properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death and serious illness in the United States.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: In 1948, the Framingham Heart Study (FHS) -- under the direction of the National Heart Institute (now known as the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NHLBI) -- embarked on a novel and ambitious project in health research.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort
entities: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: At the time, little was known about the general causes of heart disease and stroke, but the death rates for CVD had been increasing steadily since the beginning of the century and had become an American epidemic.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The objective of the FHS was to identify the common factors or characteristics that contribute to CVD by following its development over a long period of time in a large group of participants who had not yet developed overt symptoms of CVD or suffered a heart attack or stroke.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort
keyphrases: development over a long period of time
participants who had not yet developed overt symptoms

properties.page_content: Design of Framingham Heart Study. In 1948, the researchers recruited 5,209 men and women between the ages of 30 and 62 from the town of Framingham, Massachusetts, and began the first round of extensive physical examinations and lifestyle interviews that they would later analyze for common patterns related to CVD development.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Since 1948, the subjects have returned to the study every two years for an examination consisting of a detailed medical history, physical examination, and laboratory tests, and in 1971, the study enrolled a second-generation cohort -- 5,124 of the original participants' adult children and their spouses -- to participate in similar examinations.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The second examination of the Offspring cohort occurred eight years after the first examination, and subsequent examinations have occurred approximately every four years thereafter.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: In April 2002 the Study entered a new phase: the enrollment of a third generation of participants, the grandchildren of the original cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The first examination of the Third Generation Study was completed in July 2005 and involved 4,095 participants.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Thus, the FHS has evolved into a prospective, community-based, three generation family study.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The FHS is a joint project of the National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute and Boston University.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort
entities: National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute
keyphrases: National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Research Areas in the Framingham Heart Study.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Over the years, careful monitoring of the FHS population has led to the identification of the major CVD risk factors -- high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, smoking, obesity, diabetes, and physical inactivity -- as well as a great deal of valuable information on the effects of related factors such as blood triglyceride and HDL cholesterol levels, age, gender, and psychosocial issues.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Risk factors have been identified for the major components of CVD, including coronary heart disease, stroke, intermittent claudication, and heart failure.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: It is also clear from research in the FHS and other studies that substantial subclinical vascular disease occurs in the blood vessels, heart and brain that precedes clinical CVD.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: With recent advances in technology, the FHS has enhanced its research capabilities and capitalized on its inherent resources by the conduct of high resolution imaging to detect and quantify subclinical vascular disease in the major blood vessels, heart and brain.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: These studies have included ultrasound studies of the heart (echocardiography) and carotid arteries, computed tomography studies of the heart and aorta, and magnetic resonance imaging studies of the brain, heart, and aorta.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Although the Framingham cohort is primarily white, the importance of the major CVD risk factors identified in this group have been shown in other studies to apply almost universally among racial and ethnic groups, even though the patterns of distribution may vary from group to group.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: In the past half century, the Study has produced approximately 1,200 articles in leading medical journals.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The concept of CVD risk factors has become an integral part of the modern medical curriculum and has led to the development of effective treatment and preventive strategies in clinical practice.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: In addition to research studies focused on risk factors, subclinical CVD and clinically apparent CVD, Framingham investigators have also collaborated with leading researchers from around the country and throughout the world on projects involving some of the major chronic illnesses in men and women, including dementia, osteoporosis and arthritis, nutritional deficiencies, eye diseases, hearing disorders, and chronic obstructive lung diseases.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Genetic Research in the Framingham Heart Study.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: While pursuing the Study's established research goals, the NHLBI and the Framingham investigators has expanded its research mission into the study of genetic factors underlying CVD and other disorders.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Over the past two decades, DNA has been collected from blood samples and from immortalized cell lines obtained from Original Cohort participants, members of the Offspring Cohort and the Third Generation Cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Several large-scale genotyping projects have been conducted in the past decade.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Genome-wide linkage analysis has been conducted using genotypes of approximately 400 microsatellite markers that have been completed in over 9,300 subjects in all three generations.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Analyses using microsatellite markers completed in the original cohort and offspring cohorts have resulted in over 100 publications, including many publications from the Genetics Analysis Workshop 13.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Several other recent collaborative projects have completed thousands of SNP genotypes for candidate gene regions in subsets of FHS subjects with available DNA.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: These projects include the Cardiogenomics Program of the NHLBI's Programs for Genomics Applications, the genotyping of ~3000 SNPs in inflammation genes, and the completion of a genome-wide scan of 100,000 SNPs using the Affymetrix 100K Genechip.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Framingham Cohort Phenotype Data. The phenotype database contains a vast array of phenotype information available in all three generations.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: These will include the quantitative measures of the major risk factors such as systolic blood pressure, total and HDL cholesterol, fasting glucose, and cigarette use, as well as anthropomorphic measures such as body mass index, biomarkers such as fibrinogen and CRP, and electrocardiography measures such as the QT interval.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Many of these measures have been collected repeatedly in the original and offspring cohorts.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: Also included in the SHARe database will be an array of recently collected biomarkers, subclinical disease imaging measures, clinical CVD outcomes as well as an array of ancillary studies.
properties.title: Framingham Cohort

properties.page_content: The phenotype data is located here in the top-level study phs000007 Framingham Cohort.

properties.page_content: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
entities: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is the fourth leading cause of death in the United States and the only leading cause of death that is steadily increasing in frequency.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: This project will establish a racially diverse cohort that is sufficiently large and appropriately designed for genome-wide association analysis of COPD.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: A total of 10,000 subjects will be recruited, including control smokers, definite COPD cases (GOLD Stage 2 to 4), and subjects not included in either group (GOLD 1 or GOLD-Unclassified).
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: This cohort will be used for cross-sectional analysis, although long-term longitudinal follow-up will be a future goal.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: The primary focus of the study will be genome-wide association analysis to identify the genetic risk factors that determine susceptibility for COPD and COPD-related phenotypes.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Detailed phenotyping of both cases and controls, including chest CT scan assessment of emphysema and airway disease, will allow identification of genetic determinants for the heterogeneous components of the COPD syndrome.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: The hypotheses to be studied are: 1) Precise phenotypic characterization of COPD subjects using computed tomography, as well as clinical and physiological measures, will provide data that will enable the broad COPD syndrome to be decomposed into clinically significant subtypes.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: 2) Genome-wide association studies will identify genetic determinants for COPD susceptibility that will provide insight into clinically relevant COPD subtypes.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: 3) Distinct genetic determinants influence the development of emphysema and airway disease.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: The initial phase of genome-wide association analysis included 500 COPD cases and 500 control subjects (all non-Hispanic White) genotyped with the Illumina Omni-1 chip.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: The second phase genotyped the entire study cohort using the Illumina Omni-Express chip.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Unique aspects of the study include: 1) Inclusion of large numbers of African American subjects (approximately 1/3 of the cohort); 2) Obtaining chest CT scans (including inspiratory and expiratory images); and 3) Inclusion of the full range of disease severity.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene) Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The Women's Health Initiative (WHI) is a long-term national health study that has focused on strategies for preventing heart disease, breast and colorectal cancer, and osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The original WHI study included 161,808 postmenopausal women enrolled between 1993 and 1998.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center in Seattle, WA serves as the WHI Clinical Coordinating Center for data collection, management, and analysis of the WHI.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The WHI has two major parts: a partial factorial randomized Clinical Trial (CT) and an Observational Study (OS); both were conducted at 40 Clinical Centers nationwide.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The CT enrolled 68,132 postmenopausal women between the ages of 50-79 into trials testing three prevention strategies.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: If eligible, women could choose to enroll in one, two, or all three of the trial components.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The components are:  Hormone Therapy Trials (HT): This double-blind component examined the effects of combined hormones or estrogen alone on the prevention of coronary heart disease and osteoporotic fractures, and associated risk for breast cancer.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Women participating in this component with an intact uterus were randomized to estrogen plus progestin (conjugated equine estrogens [CEE], 0.625 mg/d plus medroxyprogesterone acetate [MPA] 2.5 mg/d] or a matching placebo.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Women with prior hysterectomy were randomized to CEE or placebo.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Both trials were stopped early, in July 2002 and March 2004, respectively, based on adverse effects.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: All HT participants continued to be followed without intervention until close-out.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Dietary Modification Trial (DM): The Dietary Modification component evaluated the effect of a low-fat and high fruit, vegetable and grain diet on the prevention of breast and colorectal cancers and coronary heart disease.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Study participants were randomized to either their usual eating pattern or a low-fat dietary pattern.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Calcium/Vitamin D Trial (CaD): This double-blind component began 1 to 2 years after a woman joined one or both of the other clinical trial components.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: It evaluated the effect of calcium and vitamin D supplementation on the prevention of osteoporotic fractures and colorectal cancer.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Women in this component were randomized to calcium (1000 mg/d) and vitamin D (400 IU/d) supplements or a matching placebo.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The Observational Study (OS) examines the relationship between lifestyle, environmental, medical and molecular risk factors and specific measures of health or disease outcomes.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: This component involves tracking the medical history and health habits of 93,676 women not participating in the CT.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Recruitment for the observational study was completed in 1998 and participants were followed annually for 8 to 12 years.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Extension Studies: The original protocol allowed for follow-up until March 2005, after which participants were invited to enroll in the first WHI Extension Study for follow-up through 2010.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Participants were invited again to participate in the second WHI Extension Study with continued follow up from 2010 to at least 2015.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: As of March 31, 2011 there were 93,122 women enrolled in the second extension.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: In Extension Study 2, the overall WHI study population was divided into two new subsamples, the Medical Records Cohort (MRC) and the Self-Report Cohort (SRC).
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The MRC consists of all former hormone trial participants and all African American and Hispanic participants from all study components.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The SRC consists of the remaining participants.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: The extent of outcome information collected differs between the two cohorts, with more extensive outcomes information collection on the MRC.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: As part of Extension Study 2, selected older WHI participants were invited to participate in an In Person Visit (a.k.a., Long Life Study) at their homes during which additional blood samples were collected and various measurements were taken (such as blood pressure, height, weight, waist circumference, grip strength, etc.).
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: In October 2015, Extension Study 2 was renewed with continued follow-up planned through October 2020, pending annual contract review and renewal.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Additional Information: The WHI website, https://www.whi.org/about/SitePages/About%20WHI.aspx has much more information about the study.
properties.title: Women's Health Initiative Clinical Trial and Observational Study

properties.page_content: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: MESA The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) is a study of the characteristics of subclinical cardiovascular disease (disease detected non-invasively before it has produced clinical signs and symptoms) and the risk factors that predict progression to clinically overt cardiovascular disease or progression of the subclinical disease.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: MESA researchers study a diverse, population-based sample of 6,814 asymptomatic men and women aged 45-84.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Thirty-eight percent of the recruited participants are white, 28 percent African-American, 22 percent Hispanic, and 12 percent Asian, predominantly of Chinese descent.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Participants were recruited from six field centers across the United States: Wake Forest University, Columbia University, Johns Hopkins University, University of Minnesota, Northwestern University and University of California - Los Angeles.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Each participant received an extensive physical exam and determination of coronary calcification, ventricular mass and function, flow-mediated endothelial vasodilation, carotid intimal-medial wall thickness and presence of echogenic lucencies in the carotid artery, lower extremity vascular insufficiency, arterial wave forms, electrocardiographic (ECG) measures, standard coronary risk factors, sociodemographic factors, lifestyle factors, and psychosocial factors.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Selected repetition of subclinical disease measures and risk factors at follow-up visits allows study of the progression of disease.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Blood samples have been assayed for putative biochemical risk factors and stored for case-control studies.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: DNA has been extracted and lymphocytes cryopreserved (for possible immortalization) for study of candidate genes and possibly, genome-wide scanning, expression, and other genetic techniques.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Participants are being followed for identification and characterization of cardiovascular disease events, including acute myocardial infarction and other forms of coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and congestive heart failure; for cardiovascular disease interventions; and for mortality.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: In addition to the six Field Centers, MESA involves a Coordinating Center, a Central Laboratory, and Central Reading Centers for Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Ultrasound, and Electrocardiography (ECG).
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Protocol development, staff training, and pilot testing were performed in the first 18 months of the study.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: The first examination took place over two years, from July 2000 - July 2002.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: It was followed by four examination periods that were 17-20 months in length.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: Participants have been contacted every 9 to 12 months throughout the study to assess clinical morbidity and mortality.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: MESA Family The general goal of the MESA Family Study, an ancillary study to MESA funded by a grant from NHLBI, is to apply modern genetic analysis and genotyping methodologies to delineate the genetic determinants of early atherosclerosis.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: This is being accomplished by utilizing all the current organizational structures of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) and Genetic Centers at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and University of Virginia.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: In the MESA Family Study, the goal is to locate and identify genes contributing to the genetic risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), by looking at the early changes of atherosclerosis within families (mainly siblings).
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: 2128 individuals from 594 families, yielding 3,026 sibpairs divided between African Americans and Hispanic-Americans, were recruited by utilizing the existing framework of MESA.
properties.title: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Cohort

properties.page_content: The Cleveland Family Study is the largest family-based study of sleep apnea world-wide, consisting of 2284 individuals (46% African American) from 361 families studied on up to 4 occasions over a period of 16 years.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: The study was begun in 1990 with the initial aims of quantifying the familial aggregation of sleep apnea.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: NIH renewals provided expansion of the original cohort (including increased minority recruitment) and longitudinal follow-up, with the last exam occurring in February 2006.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Index probands (n=275) were recruited from 3 area hospital sleep labs if they had a confirmed diagnosis of sleep apnea and at least 2 first-degree relatives available to be studied.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: In the first 5 years of the study, neighborhood control probands (n=87) with at least 2 living relatives available for study were selected at random from a list provided by the index family and also studied.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: All available first degree relatives and spouses of the case and control probands also were recruited.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Second-degree relatives, including half-sibs, aunts, uncles and grandparents, were also included if they lived near the first degree relatives (cases or controls), or if the family had been found to have two or more relatives with sleep apnea.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Blood was sampled and DNA isolated for participants seen in the last two exam cycles (n=1447).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: The sample, which is enriched with individuals with sleep apnea, also contains a high prevalence of individuals with sleep apnea-related traits, including: obesity, impaired glucose tolerance, and HTN.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Phenotyping data have been collected over 4 exam cycles, each occurring ~every 4 years.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: The last three exams targeted all subjects who had been studied at earlier exams, as well as new minority families and family members of previously studied probands who had been unavailable at prior exams.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Data from one, two, three and four visits are available for 412, 630, 329 and 67, participants, respectively.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: In the first 3 exams, participants underwent overnight in-home sleep studies, allowing determination of the number and duration of hypopneas and apneas, sleep period, heart rate, and oxygen saturation levels; anthropometry (weight, height, and waist, hip, and neck circumferences); resting blood pressure; spirometry; standardized questionnaire evaluation of symptoms, medications, sleep patterns, quality of life, daytime sleepiness measures and health history; venipuncture and measurement of total and HDL cholesterol.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: The 4th exam (2001-2006) was designed to collect more detailed measurements of sleep, metabolic and CVD phenotypes and included measurement of state-of-the-art polysomnography, with both collection of blood and measurement of blood pressure before and after sleep, and anthropometry, upper airway assessments, spirometry, exhaled nitric oxide, and ECG performed the morning after the sleep study.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Data have been collected by trained research assistants or GCRC nurses following written Manuals of Procedures who were certified following standard approaches for each study procedure.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Ongoing data quality, with assessment of within or between individual drift, has been monitored on an ongoing basis, using statistical techniques as well as regular re-certification procedures.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Between and within scorer reliabilities for key sleep apnea indices have been excellent, with intra-class correlation coefficients (ICCs) exceeding 0.92 for the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Sleep staging, assessed with epoch specific comparisons, also demonstrate excellent reliability for stage identification (kappas>0.82).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: There has been no evidence of significant time trends-between or within scorers- for the AHI variables.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: We also have evaluated the night-to-night variability of the AHI and other sleep variables in 91 subjects, with each measurement made 1-3 months apart.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: There is high night to night consistency for the AHI (ICC: 0.80), the arousal index (0.76), and the % sleep time in slow-wave sleep (0.73).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: We have demonstrated the comparability of the apnea estimates (AHI) determined from limited channel studies obtained at in-home settings with in full in-laboratory polysomnography.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: In addition to our published validation study, we more recently compared the AHI in 169 Cleveland Family Study participants undergoing both assessments (in-home and in-laboratory) within one week apart.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: These showed excellent levels of agreement (ICC=0.83), demonstrating the feasibility of examining data from either in-home or in-laboratory studies for apnea phenotyping.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: Data collected in the GCRC were obtained, when possible, with comparable, if not identical techniques, as were the same measures collected at prior exams performed in the participants' homes.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: To address the comparability of data collected over different exams, we calculated the crude age-adjusted correlations ~3 year within individual correlations between measures made in the most recent GCRC exam with measures made in a prior exam and demonstrated excellent levels of agreement for BMI (r=.91); waist circumference (0.91); FVC (0.88); and FEV1 (0.86).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: As expected due to higher biological and measurement variability, 149 somewhat lower 3-year correlations were demonstrated for SBP (0.56); Diastolic BP (0.48); AHI (0.62); and nocturnal oxygen desaturation (0.60).
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: NHLBI Candidate-gene Association Resource. The NHLBI initiated the Candidate gene Association Resource (CARe) to create a shared genotype/phenotype resource for analyses of the association of genotypes with phenotypes relevant to the mission of the NHLBI.
properties.title: NHLBI Cleveland Family Study (CFS) Candidate Gene Association Resource (CARe)

properties.page_content: The resource comprises nine cohort studies funded by the NHLBI: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC), Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS), Cleveland Family Study (CFS), Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA), Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease (CSSCD), Framingham Heart Study (FHS), Jackson Heart Study (JHS), Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), and the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS).

properties.page_content: CARDIA is a study examining the etiology and natural history of cardiovascular disease beginning in young adulthood.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: In 1985-1986, a cohort of 5115 healthy black and white men and women aged 18-30 years were selected to have approximately the same number of people in subgroups of age (18-24 and 25-30), sex, race, and education (high school or less and more than high school) within each of four US Field Centers.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort
keyphrases: healthy black and white men and women

properties.page_content: These same participants were asked to participate in follow-up examinations during 1987-1988 (Year 2), 1990-1991 (Year 5), 1992-1993 (Year 7), 1995-1996 (Year 10), 2000-2001 (Year 15), 2005-2006 (Year 20), and 2010-2011 (Year 25); the proportions of the surviving cohort that have returned for the seven follow-up examinations were 90%, 86%, 81%, 79%, 74%, 72%, and 72%, respectively.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: In addition to the follow-up examinations, participants are contacted regularly for the ascertainment of information on out-patient procedures and hospitalizations experienced between contacts.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: Within the past five years, 95% of the original surviving cohort has been contacted.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: While the specifics of each examination has differed somewhat, data have been collected on a variety of factors believed to be related to heart disease.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: These include conditions with clear links to heart disease such as blood pressure, cholesterol and other lipids.
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: Data have also been collected on physical measurements such as weight and skinfold fat as well as lifestyle factors such as substance use (tobacco and alcohol), dietary and exercise patterns, behavioral and psychological variables, medical and family history, and other chemistries (e.g., insulin and glucose).
properties.title: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) Study - Cohort

properties.page_content: In addition, subclinical atherosclerosis was measured via echocardiography during Years 5, 10, and 25, computed tomography during Years 15 and 20, and carotid ultrasound during Year 20.

properties.page_content: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort. The Jackson Heart Study (JHS) is a large, community-based, observational study whose participants were recruited from urban and rural areas of the three counties (Hinds, Madison and Rankin) that make up the Jackson, MS metropolitan statistical area (MSA).
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Participants were enrolled from each of 4 recruitment pools: (1) random, 17%, (2) volunteer, 30%, (3) currently enrolled in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study, 31%, and (4) secondary family members, 22%.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: The final cohort of 5,306 participants included 6.59% of all African American Jackson MSA residents, aged 35-84, during the baseline exam (N-76,426, US Census 2000).
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Among these, approximately 3,600 gave consent that allows genetic research and deposition of data into dbGaP.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Major components of three clinic examinations (see study history) include medical history, physical examination, blood/urine analytes, and interview questions on areas such as physical activity, stress, coping and spirituality, racism and discrimination, socioeconomic position, and access to health care.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Extensive clinical phenotyping includes anthropometrics, electrocardiography, carotid ultrasound, ankle-brachial blood pressure index, echocardiography, CT chest and abdomen for coronary and aortic calcification, liver fat, and subcutaneous and visceral fat measurements, and cardiac MRI.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: At 12-month intervals after the baseline clinic visit (Exam 1), participants have been contacted by telephone to update information, confirm vital statistics, document interim medical events, hospitalizations and functional status, and obtain additional sociocultural information.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Questions about medical events, symptoms of cardiovascular disease and functional status are repeated annually.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: Ongoing cohort surveillance includes abstraction of medical records and death certificates for relevant International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes and adjudication of nonfatal events and deaths.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.page_content: CMS data are currently being incorporated into the dataset.
properties.title: Jackson Heart Study (JHS) Cohort

properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Overview: Our overall long-term goal is to determine risk factors for the complex (multifactorial) disease, venous thromboembolism (VTE), that will allow physicians to stratify individual patient risk and target VTE prophylaxis to those who would benefit most.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: In this genome-wide association case-control study (1300 cases and 1300 controls) we hope to identify susceptibility variants for VTE.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Mutations within genes encoding for important components of the anticoagulant, procoagulant, fibrinolytic, and innate immunity pathways are risk factors for VTE.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: We hypothesize that other genes within these four pathways or within other pathways also are VTE disease-susceptibility genes.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Therefore, we performed a genome wide association (GWA) screen and analysis using the Illumina 660W platform to identify SNPs within 1,300 clinic-based, non-cancer VTE cases primarily from Minnesota and the upper Midwest USA, and 1300 clinic-based, unrelated controls frequency-matched on patient age, gender, myocardial infarction/stroke status and state of residence.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: This is a subset of a slightly larger candidate gene study using 1500 case-control pairs to identify haplotype-tagging SNPs (ht-SNPs) in a large set of candidate genes (n~750) within the anticoagulant, procoagulant, fibrinolytic, and innate immunity pathways.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Study Populations. Cases. VTE cases were consecutive Mayo Clinic outpatients with objectively-diagnosed deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and/or pulmonary embolism (PE) residing in the upper Midwest and referred by Mayo Clinic physician to the Mayo Clinic Special Coagulation Laboratory for clinical diagnostic testing to evaluate for an acquired or inherited thrombophilia, or to the Mayo Clinic Thrombophilia Center.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Any person contacted to be a control but discovered to have had a VTE was evaluated for inclusion as a case.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.page_content: Cases were primarily residents from Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, Illinois, North or South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri and Indiana.

properties.page_content: A DVT or PE was categorized as objectively diagnosed when (a) confirmed by venography or pulmonary angiography, or pathology examination of thrombus removed at surgery, or (b) if at least one non-invasive test (compression duplex ultrasonography, lung scan, computed tomography scan, magnetic resonance imaging) was positive.
properties.title: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) GENEVA Genome-Wide Association Study of Venous Thrombosis (GWAS of VTE)

properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: This program has conducted     over 21,000 physical examinations, assembled a shared database of several hundred BP and hypertension-related phenotypic measurements,     completed genome-wide linkage analyses for BP, hypertension, and hypertension associated risk factors and complications, and published     over 130 manuscripts on program findings.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The FBPP emerged from what was initially funded as four independent networks of investigators     (HyperGEN, GenNet, SAPPHIRe and GENOA) competing to identify genetic determinants of hypertension in multiple ethnic groups.

properties.page_content: Analysis of the molecular etiologies of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) has led to important insights into the control of immune cell development.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: Most cases of SCID result from either X-linked or autosomal recessive inheritance of mutations in a known causative gene.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: However, in some cases, the molecular etiology remains unclear.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: To identify the cause of SCID in a patient known to lack the protein tyrosine phosphatase CD45, we utilized single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNP) arrays and whole exome sequencing.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: The patient's mother was heterozygous for an inactivating mutation in CD45, while the paternal alleles lacked mutations.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: The patient exhibited a single CD45 mutation identical to the maternal allele.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: Patient SNP array analysis revealed no change in copy number but loss of heterozygosity for the entire length of chromosome 1 (Chr1), indicating that disease was caused by uniparental disomy (UPD) with isodisomy of the entire maternal Chr1 bearing the CD45 mutation.
properties.title: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute Exome sequencing in SCID

properties.page_content: These findings represent the first reported case of SCID caused by UPD and suggest UPD should be considered in SCID and other recessive disorders, especially when the patient appears homozygous for an abnormal gene found in only one parent.

properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Family Studies (Mendelian Lipid Disorders)

properties.page_content: The NHLBI "Grand Opportunity" Exome Sequencing Project (GO-ESP), a signature project of the NHLBI Recovery Act investment, was designed to identify genetic variants in coding regions (exons) of the human genome (the "exome") that are associated with heart, lung and blood diseases.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: These and related diseases that are of high impact to public health and individuals from diverse racial and ethnic groups will be studied.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: These data may help researchers understand the causes of disease, contributing to better ways to prevent, diagnose, and treat diseases, as well as determine whether to tailor prevention and treatments to specific populations.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: This could lead to more effective treatments and reduce the likelihood of side effects.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: GO-ESP is comprised of five collaborative components: 3 cohort consortia - HeartGO, LungGO, and WHISP - and 2 sequencing centers - BroadGO and SeattleGO.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: As part of this initiative, the Broad has performed genotyping on several thousand subjects from 4 different cohorts on Illumina's ExomeChip platform as described below:  The Duke Study: The Duke study enrolled cases from the Duke University Medical Center with myocardial infarction or coronary artery stenosis > 50%.
properties.title: NHLBI GO-ESP: Early-Onset Myocardial Infarction Exome Chip (Broad EOMI)

properties.page_content: Controls were individuals who were > 50 years old without coronary stenosis > 30% and without history of myocardial infarction, coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, or heart transplant.

properties.page_content: The InterMountain Heart Study: The Intermountain Heart Study is an observational registry of individuals with coronary artery disease and healthy controls who received care at participating Intermountain Healthcare facilities.

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.page_content: A total of 10,720 subjects were recruited, including control smokers and nonsmokers, definite COPD cases (GOLD Stage 2 to 4), and subjects not included in either group (GOLD 1 and PRISm).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.page_content: This cohort is being used for cross-sectional analysis, and long-term longitudinal follow-up visits after five years and after ten years are also being performed.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.page_content: The primary focus of the study is to identify the genetic risk factors that determine susceptibility for COPD and COPD-related phenotypes.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.page_content: Detailed phenotyping of both cases and controls, including chest CT scan assessment of emphysema and airway disease, will allow identification of genetic determinants for the heterogeneous components of the COPD syndrome.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.page_content: The aims for this study are:  Precise phenotypic characterization of COPD subjects using computed tomography, as well as clinical and physiological measures, that will provide data to enable the broad COPD syndrome to be decomposed into clinically significant subtype; Genome-wide association studies will identify genetic determinants for COPD susceptibility that will provide insight into clinically relevant COPD subtypes; Distinct genetic determinants influence the development of emphysema and airway disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD (COPDGene)

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: The CFS was designed to provide fundamental epidemiological data on genetic and non-genetic risk factors for sleep disordered breathing (SDB).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: In brief, the CFS is a family-based study that enrolled a total of 2284 individuals from 361 families between 1990 and 2006.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: The sample was selected by identifying affected probands who had laboratory diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: All first degree relatives, spouses and available second degree relatives of affected probands were studied.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: In addition, during the first 5 study years, neighborhood control families were identified through a neighborhood proband, and his/her spouses and first degree relatives.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Each exam, occurring at approximately 4 year intervals, included new enrollment as well as follow up exams for previously enrolled subjects.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: For the first three visits, data, including an overnight sleep study, were collected in the participants' homes while the last visit occurred in a general clinical research center (GCRC).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Phenotypic characterization of the entire cohort included overnight sleep apnea studies, blood pressure, spirometry, anthropometry and questionnaires.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: The GCRC exam (n=735 selected individuals) included more comprehensive phenotype data on a focused subsample of the larger cohort, to permit linking SDB phenotypes with cardio-metabolic phenotypes, with an interest in identifying genetic loci that are associated with these related phenotypes.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: In this last round of data collection, a subset of 735 individuals was selected based on expected genetic informativity by choosing pedigrees where siblings had extremes of the apnea hypopnea index (AHI).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Participants underwent detailed phenotyping including laboratory polysomnography (PSG), ECG, spirometry, nasal and oral acoustic reflectometry, vigilance testing, and blood and urine collection before and after sleep and after an oral glucose tolerance test.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: A wide range of biochemical measures of inflammation and metabolism were assayed by a Core Laboratory at the University of Vermont.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: 994 individuals were sequenced as part of TOPMed Phase 1, including 507 African-Americans and 487 European-Americans.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Among the sequenced individuals, 156 were probands with diagnosed sleep apnea, an additional 706 were members of families with probands, and 132 were from neighborhood control families.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: 298 individuals were sequenced as part of TOPMed Phase 3.5, including 169 African-Americans and 129 European-Americans.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Among the newly sequenced individuals, 33 were probands with diagnosed sleep apnea, an additional 214 were members of families with probands, and 51 were from neighborhood control families.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: The Amish Complex Disease Research Program includes a set of large community-based studies focused largely on cardiometabolic health carried out in the Old Order Amish (OOA) community of Lancaster, Pennsylvania (http://medschool.umaryland.edu/endocrinology/amish/research-program.asp).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: The OOA population of Lancaster County, PA immigrated to the Colonies from Western Europe in the early 1700's.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: There are now over 30,000 OOA individuals in the Lancaster area, nearly all of whom can trace their ancestry back 12-14 generations to approximately 700 founders.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: Investigators at the University of Maryland School of Medicine have been studying the genetic determinants of cardiometabolic health in this population since 1993.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish
entities: University of Maryland School of Medicine
keyphrases: University of Maryland School of Medicine

properties.page_content: To date, over 7,000 Amish adults have participated in one or more of our studies.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: Due to their ancestral history, the OOA may be enriched for rare variants that arose in the population from a single founder (or small number of founders) and propagated through genetic drift.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: Many of these variants have large effect sizes and identifying them can lead to new biological insights about health and disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: The parent study for this WGS project provides one (of multiple) examples.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: In our parent study, we identified through a genome-wide association analysis a haplotype that was highly enriched in the OOA that is associated with very high LDL-cholesterol levels.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetics of Cardiometabolic Health in the Amish

properties.page_content: At the present time, the identity of the causative SNP - and even the implicated gene - is not known because the associated haplotype contains numerous genes, none of which are obvious lipid candidate genes.

properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is an important public health problem in developed countries.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Statins are effective in the prevention and treatment of CHD; nevertheless, many patients receiving statins still suffer cardiovascular events (CV) such as heart attack.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Identifying genetic variants responsible for differential clinical responses to statins will not only allow individual patients at high residual risk to be targeted for additional therapies, but also will define new biologic pathways contributing to statin response, and thus new targets for future therapies.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Accordingly, the goal of this study is to identify genetic variants associated with clinical CV in patients receiving statins.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Subjects identified for study are of European descent and include 1718 subjects with CV while on statins (cases) and 4172 subjects without CV while on statins (controls).
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Key research resources utilized in this effort include VanderbiltD's BioVU DNA databank and associated Synthetic Derivative database of clinical information, and software tools developed to identify drugs and clinical events using Electronic Health Record-derived structured and unstructured ("free text") data.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Most cases and controls identified include three data types: ICD-9 codes, medication regimens, and medical test results.
properties.title: PGRN-RIKEN: Genetic Determinants of Clinical Cardiovascular Events in Patients Receiving Statins

properties.page_content: Since there is a greater prevalence of cardiovascular disease among African Americans, the purpose of the Jackson Heart Study (JHS) is to explore the reasons for this disparity and to uncover new approaches to reduce it.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: The JHS is a large, community-based, observational study whose 5306 participants were recruited from among the non-institutionalized African-American adults from urban and rural areas of the three counties (Hinds, Madison, and Rankin) that make up the Jackson, MS, metropolitan statistical area (MSA).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Jackson is the capital of Mississippi, the state with the largest percentage (36.3%) of African Americans in the United States.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: The JHS design included participants from the Jackson ARIC study who had originally been recruited through random selection from a drivers' license registry.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Approximately six months before the JHS was to begin, an amendment to the federal Driver's Privacy Protection Act was passed that changed the level of consent for public release of personal information from driver's license lists from an "opt out" to an "opt in" basis.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: The Mississippi Highway Patrol was no longer able to release a complete listing of all persons with driver's licenses or state identification cards, which prevented its use in the JHS.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: New JHS participants were chosen randomly from the Accudata America commercial listing, which provides householder name, address, zip code, phone number (if available), age group in decades, and family components.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: The Accudata list was deemed to provide the most complete count of households for individuals aged 55 years and older in the Jackson MSA.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: A structured volunteer sample was also included in which demographic cells for recruitment were designed to mirror the eligible population.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Enrollment was opened to volunteers who met census-derived age, sex, and socioeconomic status (SES) eligibility criteria for the Jackson MSA.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: In addition, a family component was included in the JHS.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: The sampling frame for the family study was a participant in any one of the ARlC, random, or volunteer samples whose family size met eligibility requirements.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Eligibility included having at least two full siblings and four first degree relatives (parents, siblings, children over the age of 21) who lived in the Jackson MSA and who were willing to participate in the study.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: No upper age limit was placed on the family sample.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Known contact information was obtained during the baseline clinic examination from the index family member with a verbal pedigree format to identify name(s), age(s), address (es), and telephone number(s).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Recruitment was limited to persons 35-84 years old except in the family cohort, where those 21 years old and above were eligible.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Jackson Heart Study (JHS)

properties.page_content: Only persons who otherwise met study criteria but were deemed to be physically or mentally incompetent by trained recruiters were excluded from study eligibility.1  1 Wyatt SB, Diekelmann N, Henderson F, Andrew ME, Billingsley G, Felder SH et al.

properties.page_content: The research goal of the parent study (dbGaP ID phs000914) is to identify genetic variation that increases susceptibility to obesity and cardiometabolic phenotypes among adult Samoans using genome-wide association (GWAS) methods.

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica
entities: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: We focus on asthma because of its public health significance.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Asthma affects 26 million U.S. children and adults, remains a major cause of morbidity (one-half million hospitalizations a year) and is the most common cause of school and work days lost.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Asthma-related costs are estimated to be over $12.7 billion annually.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: The Asthma Probands for both the extended pedigrees and the trios utilized in this study were selected on the basis of a physician diagnosis of asthma; a history of recurrent asthma attacks or at least 2 respiratory symptoms; and either airway hyperresponsiveness to methacholine or significant response to bronchodilator (Albuterol) administration.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: These criteria are identical to the criteria used in the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: The three primary goals of this project are to: (1) identify common and rare genetic variants that determine asthma and its associated phenotypes (height, weight, IgE level, lung function, bronchodilator response, steroid treatment response) through whole genome sequencing (WGS); (2) perform novel family based association analysis of our WGS data to identify novel genes for asthma; and (3) integrate epigenomic and transcriptomic data with our WGS data and determine the epistatic interactions present using systems genomics approaches.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Identification of the molecular determinants of asthma remains an important priority in translational science.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been successful in this regard, identifying at least 10 novel susceptibility genes for asthma.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: However, as with most complex traits, the variants identified by GWAS explain only a fraction of the estimated heritability of this disorder.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Herein, we propose a novel family-based study design and state-of-the-art genome sequencing techniques to map a set of sequence variants for asthma and its associated phenotypes and assess the interrelationships of the identified genes and variants using systems genomics methods.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: We have assembled a team of investigators highly-skilled and expert in whole genome sequencing (Drs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Michael Cho and Benjamin Raby), genetic association analysis (Drs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Scott T. Weiss, Jessica Lasky-Su and Christoph Lange), integrative genomics (Drs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Raby, Kelan Tantisira, Augusto Litonjua and Dawn DeMeo), and systems genomics (Drs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica

properties.page_content: Weiss, Amitabh Sharma, Lange and Raby) to address this important problem with both a novel study design and data set.

properties.page_content: Objectives The Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH) is a case-control study of risk factors for the development of myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, venous thrombosis (VT), and atrial fibrillation (AF).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: The study setting is Group Health, an integrated health care delivery system in Washington State.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Only VT cases and early-onset AF cases are included as part of TOPMed.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Background The HVH study originated in 1988 with the examination of risk factors for MI.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Over the ensuing years, the study has been funded by a series of grants which have added case subjects with stroke, VT, and AF.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Study aims focused on the associations of medication use with cardiovascular events, and starting in 1997, the study aims expanded to include genetic associations with cardiovascular disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Participants recruited in 2009 or later who provided blood samples for genetic analysis were asked for consent to deposit genetic and phenotypic data in dbGaP.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Design As part of the HVH study, case subjects were identified by searching for ICD-9 codes consistent with MI, stroke, VT, or AF, and medical records were reviewed to confirm the diagnosis.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Control subjects were identified at random from the Group Health enrollment and were matched to MI cases.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: All subjects have an index date.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: For cases, the index date was assigned as the date that the cardiovascular event (MI, stroke, VT, or AF) came to clinical attention.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: For controls, the index date was a random date within the range of the case index dates.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: For both cases and controls, information was collected from the inpatient and outpatient medical record, by telephone interview with consenting survivors, and from the Group Health pharmacy and laboratory databases.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Consenting participants provided a blood specimen.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Subjects Only VT and early-onset AF cases from HVH are included in TOPMed.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Within the HVH study, VT and AF cases were diagnosed in both inpatient and outpatient settings, and only incident cases are eligible for inclusion in TOPMed.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: Genetic Research Genetic factors underlying cardiovascular disease are studied using DNA isolated from the blood samples.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Heart and Vascular Health Study (HVH)

properties.page_content: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: The causal mechanisms of common diseases and their therapies have been only marginally illuminated by genetic variants identified in genome wide association studies (GWAS) utilizing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNPs).
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: Platelet activation pathways reflecting hemostasis and thrombosis are the underlying substrate for many cardiovascular diseases and related acute events.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: To overcome GWAS limitations, genomic studies are needed that integrate molecular surrogates for platelet-related phenotypes assayed in cell-based models derived from individuals of known genotypes and phenotypes.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: In our GWAS study of native platelet aggregation phenotypes and aggregation in response to low dose aspirin in 2200 subjects (GeneSTAR, Genetic Study of Aspirin Responsiveness), important genome wide "signals" (p<5x10-8) associated with native platelet aggregation and important "signals" associated with platelet responsiveness to aspirin were identified and replicated.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: Although we are currently performing functional genomics studies to elucidate our most promising findings in known genes (PEAR1, MET, PIKC3G), most "signals" occurred in intergenic regions or in introns.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: Mechanistic interpretation is limited by uncertainty as to which gene(s) are up- or down-regulated in the presence of most SNP modifications.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: In this 3 phase proposal, we will (1) create pluripotent stem cells (iPS) from peripheral blood mononuclear cells, and then differentiate these stem cells into megakaryocytes (2) develop an efficient strategy to produce iPS and megakaryocytes using a novel pooling method, and (3) produce iPS and megakaryocytes from 250 subjects in GeneSTAR (European Americans and African Americans), selected based on specific hypotheses derived from GWAS signals in native and post aspirin platelet function; characterize genetic mRNA transcripts using a comprehensive Affymetrix array; measure protein expression for transcripts of interest using mass spectrometry; examine mRNA and protein expression patterns for each GWAS signal to determine the functional pathway(s) involved in native platelet phenotypes; and examine the functional genomics of variations in responsiveness to aspirin using our prior genotyped and phenotyped population.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.page_content: Precise information about the exact functional processes in megakaryocytes and platelets may lead to innovative and tailored approaches to risk assessment and novel therapeutic targets to prevent first and recurrent cardiovascular and related thrombotic events.
properties.title: GeneSTAR (Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk) NextGen Consortium: Functional Genomics of Platelet Aggregation Using iPS and Derived Megakaryocytes

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetics and Epidemiology of Asthma in Barbados

properties.page_content: Asthmatics of African descent tend to have more severe asthma and more severe clinical symptoms than individuals of European ancestry.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetics and Epidemiology of Asthma in Barbados

properties.page_content: The baseline prevalence of asthma in Barbados is high (~20%), and from admixture analyses, we have determined that the proportion of African ancestry among Barbadian founders is similar to U.S.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetics and Epidemiology of Asthma in Barbados

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: The Genetics and Epidemiology of Asthma in Barbados
