properties.page_content: This study aims to comprehensively interrogate the genomes of African American sarcoidosis families.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: Sarcoidosis is characterized by a hyperimmune response resulting in granuloma formation in multiple organs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: It affects African Americans (AAs) more frequently and more severely than whites.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: While previous linkage, admixture, candidate gene and genome-wide association (GWA) studies show statistically compelling effects, causal variants are still unknown and much of sarcoidosis heritability is yet to be explained.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: This "missing" heritability likely includes effects of both common (minor allele frequency (MAF)>5%) and rare variants (MAF<5%), since, in AAs, the former are inadequately represented and the latter are completely unexplored by commercial genotyping arrays.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: These facts, coupled with the availability of next-generation sequencing compel us to perform an exhaustive search for genetic variants that form the basis of sarcoidosis.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.page_content: The data generated are certain to identify candidate causal variants, provide fundamental insight for functional studies and lead to important new hypotheses of inflammation resulting in new treatments in not only sarcoidosis but other inflammatory diseases as well.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: African American Sarcoidosis Genetics Resource

properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA) is one of four networks in the NHLBI Family-Blood Pressure Program (FBPP).
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: GENOA's long-term objective is to elucidate the genetics of target organ complications of hypertension, including both atherosclerotic and arteriolosclerotic complications involving the heart, brain, kidneys, and peripheral arteries.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The longitudinal GENOA Study recruited European-American and African-American sibships with at least 2 individuals with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60 years.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: All other members of the sibship were invited to participate regardless of their hypertension status.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Participants were diagnosed with hypertension if they had either 1) a previous clinical diagnosis of hypertension by a physician with current anti-hypertensive treatment, or 2) an average systolic blood pressure ≥ 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 90 mm Hg based on the second and third readings at the time of their clinic visit.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The Family Blood Pressure Program (FBPP), GENOA's parent program, is an unprecedented collaboration to identify genes influencing blood pressure (BP) levels, hypertension, and its target-organ damage.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: This program has conducted over 21,000 physical examinations, assembled a shared database of several hundred BP and hypertension-related phenotypic measurements, completed genome-wide linkage analyses for BP, hypertension, and hypertension associated risk factors and complications, and published over 130 manuscripts on program findings.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The FBPP emerged from what was initially funded as four independent networks of investigators (HyperGEN, GenNet, SAPPHIRe and GENOA) competing to identify genetic determinants of hypertension in multiple ethnic groups.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Realizing the greater likelihood of success through collaboration, the investigators created a single confederation with program-wide and network-specific goals.
properties.title: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: ECLIPSE was a longitudinal observational study of 2164 COPD subjects and a smaller number of smoking controls (337) and nonsmoking controls (245) followed regularly for three years, with three chest CT scans (at baseline, one year, and three years) (Vestbo, European Respiratory Journal 2008; 31: 869).
properties.title: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate Endpoints (ECLIPSE)

properties.page_content: Inclusion criteria included age 40-75, at least 10 pack-years of smoking, and spirometry in GOLD grades 2-4 (COPD cases) or normal spirometry with post-bronchodilator FEV1 >85% predicted and FEV1/FVC>0.7 (controls).
properties.title: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate Endpoints (ECLIPSE)

properties.page_content: Study visits were performed at enrollment, three months, and every six months thereafter with spirometry, questionnaires, and other clinical evaluations.
properties.title: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate Endpoints (ECLIPSE)

properties.page_content: The ECLIPSE CT scans have been analyzed with the VIDA software for emphysema and airway phenotypes.
properties.title: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate Endpoints (ECLIPSE)

properties.page_content: ECLIPSE has provided key insights into the clinical epidemiology of COPD, including COPD exacerbations (Hurst, NEJM 2010; 363: 1128) and lung function decline in COPD (Vestbo, NEJM 2011; 365: 1184).
properties.title: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate Endpoints (ECLIPSE)

properties.page_content: ECLIPSE has been used in a number of genetic studies of COPD susceptibility and protein biomarkers(Faner, Thorax 2014; 69: 666).

properties.page_content: Genome-wide gene expression microarray data are available in 147 induced sputum samples from COPD subjects and 248 peripheral blood samples from COPD and control subjects.

properties.page_content: The Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA) is one of four networks in the NHLBI Family-Blood Pressure Program (FBPP).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: GENOA's long-term objective is to elucidate the genetics of target organ complications of hypertension, including both atherosclerotic and arteriolosclerotic complications involving the heart, brain, kidneys, and peripheral arteries.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The longitudinal GENOA Study recruited European-American and African-American sibships with at least 2 individuals with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60 years.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: All other members of the sibship were invited to participate regardless of their hypertension status.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Participants were diagnosed with hypertension if they had either 1) a previous clinical diagnosis of hypertension by a physician with current anti-hypertensive treatment, or 2) an average systolic blood pressure = 140 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure = 90 mm Hg based on the second and third readings at the time of their clinic visit.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Only participants of the African-American Cohort were sequenced through TOPMed.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The Family Blood Pressure Program (FBPP), GENOA's parent program, is an unprecedented collaboration to identify genes influencing blood pressure (BP) levels, hypertension, and its target-organ damage.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: This program has conducted over 21,000 physical examinations, assembled a shared database of several hundred BP and hypertension-related phenotypic measurements, completed genome-wide linkage analyses for BP, hypertension, and hypertension associated risk factors and complications, and published over 130 manuscripts on program findings.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The FBPP emerged from what was initially funded as four independent networks of investigators (HyperGEN, GenNet, SAPPHIRe and GENOA) competing to identify genetic determinants of hypertension in multiple ethnic groups.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Realizing the greater likelihood of success through collaboration, the investigators created a single confederation with program-wide and network-specific goals.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: Comprehensive phenotypic data for GENOA study participants are available through dbGaP phs001238.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy (GENOA)

properties.page_content: The GOLDN study was initiated to assess how genetic factors interact with environmental (diet and drug) interventions to influence blood levels of triglycerides and other atherogenic lipid species and inflammation markers (registered at clinicaltrials.gov, number NCT00083369).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: The study recruited Caucasian participants primarily from three-generational pedigrees from two NHLBI Family Heart Study (FHS) field centers (Minneapolis, MN and Salt Lake City, UT).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: Only families with at least two siblings were recruited and only participants who did not take lipid-lowering agents (pharmaceuticals or nutraceuticals) for at least 4 weeks prior to the initial visit were included.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate
keyphrases: families with at least two siblings

properties.page_content: The diet intervention followed the protocol of Patsch et al.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: (1992). The whipping cream (83% fat) meal had 700 Calories/m2 body surface area (2.93 mJ/m2 body surface area): 3% of calories were derived from protein (instant nonfat dry milk) and 14% from carbohydrate (sugar).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: The ratio of polyunsaturated to saturated fat was 0.06 and the cholesterol content of the average meal was 240 mg.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: The mixture was blended with ice and flavorings.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: Blood samples were drawn immediately before (fasting) and at 3.5 and 6 hours after consuming the high-fat meal.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: The diet intervention was administered at baseline as well as after a 3-week treatment with 160 mg micronized fenofibrate.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: Participants were given the option to complete one or both (diet and drug) interventions.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: GOLDN Epigenetic Determinants of Lipid Response to Dietary Fat and Fenofibrate

properties.page_content: Of all participants, 1079 had phenotypic data and provided appropriate consent, and underwent whole genome sequencing through the Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) program.

properties.page_content: The Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) is a study of the characteristics of subclinical cardiovascular disease (disease detected non-invasively before it has produced clinical signs and symptoms) and the risk factors that predict progression to clinically overt cardiovascular disease or progression of the subclinical disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: MESA researchers study a diverse, population-based sample of 6,814 asymptomatic men and women aged 45-84.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Thirty-eight percent of the recruited participants are white, 28 percent African-American, 22 percent Hispanic, and 12 percent Asian, predominantly of Chinese descent.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Comprehensive phenotypic and pedigree data for MESA study participants are available through dbGaP entry phs000209.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: MESA Participants were recruited from six field centers across the United States: Wake Forest University, Columbia University, Johns Hopkins University, University of Minnesota, Northwestern University and University of California - Los Angeles.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Each participant received an extensive physical exam and determination of coronary calcification, ventricular mass and function, flow-mediated endothelial vasodilation, carotid intimal-medial wall thickness and presence of echogenic lucencies in the carotid artery, lower extremity vascular insufficiency, arterial wave forms, electrocardiographic (ECG) measures, standard coronary risk factors, sociodemographic factors, lifestyle factors, and psychosocial factors.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Selected repetition of subclinical disease measures and risk factors at follow-up visits allows study of the progression of disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Blood samples have been assayed for putative biochemical risk factors and stored for case-control studies.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: DNA has been extracted and lymphocytes cryopreserved (for possible immortalization) for study of candidate genes and possibly, genome-wide scanning, expression, and other genetic techniques.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Participants are being followed for identification and characterization of cardiovascular disease events, including acute myocardial infarction and other forms of coronary heart disease (CHD), stroke, and congestive heart failure; for cardiovascular disease interventions; and for mortality.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: In addition to the six Field Centers, MESA involves a Coordinating Center, a Central Laboratory, and Central Reading Centers for Computed Tomography (CT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Ultrasound, and Electrocardiography (ECG).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Protocol development, staff training, and pilot testing were performed in the first 18 months of the study.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: The first examination took place over two years, from July 2000 - July 2002.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: It was followed by five examination periods that were 17-20 months in length.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Participants have been contacted every 9 to 12 months throughout the study to assess clinical morbidity and mortality.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: MESA Family The general goal of the MESA Family Study, an ancillary study to MESA funded by a grant from NHLBI, is to apply modern genetic analysis and genotyping methodologies to delineate the genetic determinants of early atherosclerosis.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: This is being accomplished by utilizing all the current organizational structures of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) and Genetic Centers at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center and University of Virginia.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: In the MESA Family Study, the goal is to locate and identify genes contributing to the genetic risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), by looking at the early changes of atherosclerosis within families (mainly siblings).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: 2128 individuals from 594 families, yielding 3,026 sibpairs divided between African Americans and Hispanic-Americans, were recruited by utilizing the existing framework of MESA.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: MESA Family studied siblings of index subjects from the MESA study and from new sibpair families (with the same demographic characteristics) and is determining the extent of genetic contribution to the variation in coronary calcium (obtained via CT Scan) and carotid artery wall thickness (B-mode ultrasound) in the two largest non-majority U.S.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: populations. In a small proportion of subjects, parents of MESA index subjects participating in MESA Family were studied but only to have blood drawn for genotyping.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: The MESA Family cohort was recruited from the six MESA Field Centers.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: MESA Family participants underwent the same examination as MESA participants during May 2004 - May 2007.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: DNA was extracted and lymphocytes immortalized for study of candidate genes, genome-wide linkage scanning, and analyzed for linkage with these subclinical cardiovascular traits.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: While linkage analysis is the primary approach being used, an additional aspect of the MESA Family Study takes advantage of the existing MESA study population for testing a variety of candidate genes for association with the same subclinical traits.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: Genotyping and data analysis will occur throughout the study.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: MESA and MESA Family AA-CAC

properties.page_content: The UMMS miRhythm Study is an ongoing study of adult patients undergoing an elective electrophysiology study or arrhythmia ablation procedure for a supraventricular or ventricular arrhythmia, including atrial fibrillation (AF).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: Atrial fibrillation is a major clinical and public health problem that is related to atrial pathologic remodeling.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: Few tools are available to quantify the activity or extent of this remodeling, rendering it difficult to identify individuals at risk for AF.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: Previous studies have suggested an important role for miRNA in cardiovascular disease through gene expression regulation, making this a promising avenue for studying AF mechanisms.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: The aim of the study is to determine the time-dependent changes to key circulating miRNAs in a model of planned atrial injury and remodeling via ablation.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: Such knowledge might provide additional insight into the biology and activity of the acute atrial injury response, and furthermore, inform new targets for development of preventative interventions or allow for better AF risk stratification.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: To assess pathways regulating atrial pathological remodeling, patient blood samples are collected prior to their ablation procedures and also at a regularly scheduled 1-month follow-up appointment.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: Plasma expression of miRNA is measured using high-throughput quantitative reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), providing novel insights into the regulatory processes underlying AF, as well as acute atrial injury in vivo.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias
keyphrases: high-throughput quantitative reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction

properties.page_content: Additionally, data collected from whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is used to supplement miRNA analyses and further explore new relations between genes and abnormal heart rhythm.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Defining the Time-Dependent Genetic and Transcriptomic Responses to Cardiac Injury Among Patients with Arrhythmias

properties.page_content: The REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort study focused on transfusion practices and predictors of health outcomes in patients with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) and began in the Fall of 2013.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort (REDS-BSCDC)

properties.page_content: The four primary aims of this study are: 1) Aim A - Establish a cohort of SCD patients with a comprehensive centralized electronic database of detailed clinical, laboratory and transfusion information, as well as establish a repository of blood samples to support biological studies relevant to SCD pathogenesis and transfusion complications; 2) Aim B - Characterize changes in markers of inflammation in response to transfusion by analyzing chemokine/cytokine panels in serial post transfusion specimens; 3) Aim C - Identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that contribute to the risk of red blood cell alloimmunization in SCD by performing a genome-wide association (GWA) study in transfused SCD patients; and, 4) Aim D - Characterize risk of HIV and HIV outcomes in the Brazilian SCD population and compare SCD outcomes among HIV sero-positive and sero-negative SCD patients.

properties.page_content: Hemophilia is clinically categorized by coagulation factor activity levels and ranges in severity from mild (6% to 30%) to moderate (1-5%) to severe (<1%).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Many female "carriers" of hemophilia also have decreased factor activity and morbidity from bleeding.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Hemophilia A and B are almost always caused by identifiable mutations in the F8 and F9 genes, respectively, and these mutations are found throughout the structural genes.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Although the hemophilias are monogenic disorders, there are wide variations in disease severity and therapeutic outcomes which are not readily explained by the disease causing mutations alone.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: The My Life Our Future (MLOF) project (www.mylifeourfuture.org) is a national resource developed by a partnership of BloodworksNW (BWNW, formerly the Puget Sound Blood Center), the American Thrombosis and Hemostasis Network (ATHN), the National Hemophilia Foundation (NHF) and Bioverativ, to provide free F8 and F9 gene variant analysis to patients with hemophilia A or B, and to establish a research repository of DNA sequence, DNA, RNA, buffy coat, serum and plasma.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)
keyphrases: F8 and F9 gene variant analysis

properties.page_content: The sequence analysis and serum samples are linked to a phenotypic database hosted by ATHN, with samples submitted and clinical data entered at ~100 hemophilia treatment centers (HTCs) nationwide.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: (See ATHN Research Report Brief in the resource center at www.athn.org).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: MLOF has become the largest hemophilia genetic project worldwide.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: The roles of the MLOF partners are: BWNW, to serve as the central laboratory for the project and house the research repository; ATHN, to support and provide the administrative link with HTCs, to facilitate the collection of accurate phenotypic data, to conduct research review and approval for use of the repository and with BWNW to provide samples and data for research projects; NHF, to provide consumer education and facilitate consumer input into the project; and Bioverativ, to provide financial support and scientific input.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: The project is governed by a Steering Committee consisting of one representative from each organization.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Subject samples chosen from the MLOF parent study for TOPMed and WGS were drawn from those who gave (or parents gave) informed consent for the Research Repository and included patients of all severities and type, but with an emphasis on those with severe hemophilia and others at increased risk of neutralizing antibody (inhibitor) formation and who had samples in the Research Repository (plasma, serum, RNA) for potential additional -omic studies.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Also included were samples from subjects where a likely causative variant for hemophilia was not found in the F8 or F9 coding region, intron-exon boundaries or immediate upstream and downstream regions.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Since hemophilia is an X-linked disorder, the majority of subjects are male.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: My Life Our Future (MLOF) Research Repository of Patients with Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) or Hemophilia B (Factor IX Deficiency)

properties.page_content: Racial distribution is similar to the overall population distribution.

properties.page_content: Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia, is the primary cause of many hospital admissions, and is associated with significant secondary morbidity by increasing the risk of stroke, heart failure, and all-cause mortality.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: The incidence of AF is on the rise, and it is projected that by the year 2050 more than 10 million patients will be affected by AF in the United States alone.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Anti-arrhythmic medications have limited success in maintaining sinus rhythm, are associated with side effects, and appear ineffective at reducing mortality compared to a strategy of rate control and anticoagulation.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Given the significant morbidity associated with this common arrhythmia, surgical and catheter ablation techniques have been developed to treat AF.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: However, despite the incorporation of various strategies for ablation, long-term recurrence rates of AF remain higher than 25 percent after ablation.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Current techniques for catheter ablation of AF include pulmonary vein isolation and complex fractionated atrial electrogram (CFAE) ablation.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: However, the contribution of each strategy to long-term procedural success and the relative importance of each strategy for different patients remain unknown.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Recent advances in cardiac imaging have allowed detailed analysis of left atrial myocardial anatomy.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Parallel advances in molecular genetics have identified several candidate genes involved in familial and non-familial AF.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: However, the pathophysiology of AF generation and maintenance, and the potential contribution of such genetic or anatomic substrates for patient selection, and for target identification during catheter ablation have not yet been examined.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: Advances in molecular genetics and imaging, coupled with techniques for endocardial and epicardial mapping in the electrophysiology laboratory present an opportunity to significantly improve our understanding of (1) The relation of paroxysmal versus persistent AF with (a) structural left atrial changes (left/right atrial scar, wall thinning, pulmonary vein anomalies, and coronary sinus dilation) and with (b) candidate genetic variants.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: (2) The relation of candidate genetic variants with (a) structural left atrial changes and with (b) electrophysiologic properties (atrial effective refractory period (AERP) inhomogeneity, voltage abnormalities, trigger burden and location, C FAE extent and location), (3) The relation of structural left atrial changes with (a) CFAE location as targets for catheter ablation and with (b) reversible conduction block/myocardial injury after pulmonary vein isolation, and (4) Individualized endocardial targets for AF ablation based on candidate genes and anatomic substrates.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.page_content: The proposed study will improve our understanding of the underlying pathophysiology of AF, and may improve current techniques for treatment of this important arrhythmia.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine Atrial Fibrillation Genetics Study

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is caused by homozygosity for a single mutation of the beta hemoglobin gene.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: Despite the constancy of this genetic abnormality, the clinical course of patients with SCD is remarkably variable.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: SCD can affect the function and cause the failure of multiple organ systems through the pathophysiologic processes of vaso-occlusion and hemolysis.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: These pathophysiological processes are complex and expected to impact multiple organ systems in a variety of ways.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: This study, therefore, was designed to identify genetic factors that predispose SCD patients to develop specific end-organ complications and to experience more or less severe clinical courses.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: We enrolled > 700 patients with Hb SS, Hb S-beta0 thalassemia and HbSC being followed primarily at three southeastern U.S.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: regional institutions (Duke University Medical Center, University of North Carolina Medical Center, and Emory University Medical Center).

keyphrases: University of North Carolina Medical Center

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Outcome Modifying Genes in Sickle Cell Disease (OMG)

properties.page_content: Clinical data include medical status (history, physical, examination, and laboratory results) and information regarding potentially confounding environmental factors.

properties.page_content: (2014), PMID: 24478166. Clinical and genetic data have been used to identify genetic characteristics predisposing patients with SCD to a more or less severe overall clinical course as well as to individual organ-specific complications.

properties.page_content: It is anticipated that identification of such genetic factors will reveal new therapeutic targets individualized to specific complications of SCD, leading to improved outcomes and increased life expectancy for patients with SCD.

properties.page_content: CARDIA is a study examining the etiology and natural history of cardiovascular disease beginning in young adulthood.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: In 1985-1986, a cohort of 5115 healthy black and white men and women, aged 18-30 years, were selected to have approximately the same number of people in subgroups of age (18-24 and 25-30), sex, race, and education (high school or less, and more than high school) within each of four US Field Centers.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)
keyphrases: healthy black and white men and women

properties.page_content: These same participants were asked to participate in follow-up examinations during 1987-1988 (Year 2), 1990-1991 (Year 5), 1992-1993 (Year 7), 1995-1996 (Year 10), 2000-2001 (Year 15), 2005-2006 (Year 20), 2010-2011 (Year 25) and 2015-2016 (Year 30).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: In addition to the follow-up examinations, participants are contacted regularly for the ascertainment of information on out-patient procedures and hospitalizations experienced between contacts.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: Within the past five years, 95% of the original surviving cohort has been contacted.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: While the specifics of each examination have differed somewhat, data have been collected on a variety of factors believed to be related to heart disease.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: These include conditions with clear links to heart disease, such as blood pressure, cholesterol and other lipids.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: Data have also been collected on physical measurements, such as weight and skinfold fat, as well as lifestyle factors such as substance use (tobacco and alcohol), dietary and exercise patterns, behavioral and psychological variables, medical and family history, and other chemistries (e.g., insulin and glucose).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA)

properties.page_content: In addition, subclinical atherosclerosis was measured via echocardiography during Years 5, 10, and 25, computed tomography during Years 15 and 20, and carotid ultrasound during Year 20.Comprehensive phenotypic data for study participants are available through dbGaP phs000285.

properties.page_content: The IPM BioMe Biobank, founded in September 2007, is an ongoing, broadly-consented electronic health record (EHR)-linked clinical care biobank that enrolls participants non-selectively from the Mount Sinai Medical Center patient population.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: BioMe currently comprises >42,000 participants from diverse ancestries, characterized by a broad spectrum of longitudinal biomedical traits.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Participants are enrolled through an opt-in process and consent to be followed throughout their clinical care (past, present, and future) in real-time, allowing us to integrate their genomic information with their EHRs for discovery research and clinical care implementation.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: BioMe participants consent for recall, based on their genotype and/or phenotype, permitting in-depth follow-up and functional studies for selected participants at any time.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Phenotypic and genomic data are stored in a secure database and made available to investigators, contingent on approval by the BioMe Governing Board.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: BioMe uses a "data-broker" system to protect confidentiality.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Ancestral diversity - BioMe participants represent a broad racial, ethnic and socioeconomic diversity with a distinct and population-specific disease burden.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Specifically, BioMe participants are of African (AA), Hispanic/Latino (HL), European (EA) and other/mixed ancestry.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: BioMe participants are predominantly of African (AA, 24%), Hispanic/Latino (HL, 35%), European (EA, 32%), and other ancestry (OA, 10%).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Participants who self-identify as Hispanic/Latino further report to be of Puerto Rican (39%), Dominican (23%), Central/South American (17%), Mexican (5%) or other Hispanic (16%) ancestry.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: More than 40% of European ancestry participants are genetically determined to be of Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: With this broad ancestral diversity, BioMe is uniquely positioned to examine the impact of demographic and evolutionary forces that have shaped common disease risk.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Phenotypes available in BioMe - BioMe has a high-quality and validated set of fully implemented clinical phenotype data that has been culled by a multi-disciplinary team of experienced investigators, clinicians, information technologists, data-managers, and programmers who apply advanced medical informatics and data mining tools to extract and harmonize EHRs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: BioMe, as a cohort, offers a great versatility for designing nested case-control sample-sets, particularly for studying longitudinal traits and co-morbidity in disease burden.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Biomedical and clinical outcomes: The BioMe Biobank is linked to Mount Sinai's system-wide Epic EHR, which captures a full spectrum of biomedical phenotypes, including clinical outcomes, covariate and exposure data from past, present and future health care encounters.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: As such, the BioMe Biobank has a longitudinal design as participants consent to make all of their EHR data from past (dating back as far as 2003), present and future inpatient or outpatient encounters available for research, without restriction.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: The median number of outpatient encounters is 21 per participant, reflecting predominant enrollment of participants with common chronic conditions from primary care facilities.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Environmental data: The clinical and EHR information is complemented by detailed demographic and lifestyle information, including ancestry, residence history, country of origin, personal and familial medical history, education, socio-economic status, physical activity, smoking, dietary habits, alcohol intake, and body weight history, which is collected in a systematic manner by interview-based questionnaire at time of enrollment.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: The IPM BioMe Biobank contributed ~10,600 DNA samples for whole genome sequencing to the TOPMed program.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Samples were selected for the Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) and the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) working groups.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Using a Case-Definition-Algorithm (CDA), we identified ~4,100 individuals with CAD (~50% women) and ~3,000 individuals as controls (65% women).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: In addition, we identified ~800 individuals with COPD (62% women) and 1800 individuals as controls (72% women).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Another 600 BioMe participants with Atrial Fibrillation, all of African ancestry, were included.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed - NHGRI CCDG: The BioMe Biobank at Mount Sinai

properties.page_content: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a disease state characterized by airflow limitation that is not fully reversible, is the third leading cause of death in the U.S.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: COPD is a heterogeneous syndrome, with affected individuals demonstrating marked differences in lung structure (emphysema vs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: airway disease); physiology (airflow obstruction); and other clinical features (e.g., exacerbations, co-morbid illnesses).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Multiple genomic regions influencing COPD susceptibility have been identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and rare coding variants can also influence risk for COPD.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: However, only a small percentage of the estimated heritability for COPD risk can be explained by known genetic loci.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Like most complex diseases, COPD is influenced by multiple genetic determinants (each with modest individual effects).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Emerging evidence supports the paradigm that complex disease genetic determinants are part of a network of interacting genes and proteins; perturbations of this network can increase disease risk.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: To identify this network, multiple Omics data will need to be analyzed with methods to account for nonlinear relationships and interactions between key genes and proteins.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Our overall hypothesis is that integrated network analysis of genetic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and epigenetic data from biospecimens ranging from lung tissue to nasal epithelial cells to blood in highly phenotyped subjects will provide insights into COPD pathogenesis and heterogeneity.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: We will leverage the well-phenotyped, NHLBI-funded Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC) to address these questions.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: We will perform multi-omics analysis in 1548 lung tissue and blood samples from the LTRC.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: With these multi-omics data, we will utilize a systems biology approach to understand relationships between multiple genetic determinants and multiple types of Omics data.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: We will begin by performing single Omics analyses in COPD vs.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: control lung, nasal, and blood samples.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Next, we will integrate single Omics data with genetic variants identified by WGS to assist in fine mapping genetic determinants of COPD.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: We will then perform integrated network analysis of COPD with genetic and multiple Omics data using correlation-based, gene regulatory, and Bayesian networks.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.page_content: Subjects were recruited from Mayo Clinic, Universities of Colorado, Michigan, and Pittsburgh, and Temple University.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Lung Tissue Research Consortium (LTRC)

properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Myocardial ischemia occurs when there is a mismatch between coronary oxygen delivery and metabolic requirements of the myocardium, which may be clinically manifested during angina, coronary angioplasty or cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB).
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Myocardial ischemia may lead to a spectrum of myocardial stunning, hibernating myocardium, and ultimately cell death if the ischemic insult is severe.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: In the human heart, irreversible damage begins after approximately 20 to 40 minutes of oxygen deprivation.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Observed molecular and cellular changes of myocardial ischemia are characteristic of an inflammatory response, but the exact mechanisms that underlie this pathological process are unclear and may not be full emulated by animal models of ischemia or infarction.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Thus, we felt it valuable to investigate a human ischemia model.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: During cardiac surgery, CPB with aortic cross-clamping (AoXC) and cardioplegic arrest is associated with excellent clinical outcomes and suitable operative conditions.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: However, despite the use of cardioprotective strategies, AoXc during CPB is accompanied by a variable, yet obligate ischemic period lasting 1 to 3 hours, resulting in hypoxia, metabolic substrate depletion, reperfusion injury, apoptosis, and necrosis.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Cardiac specific biomarkers of ischemia and infarction, including troponin, are elevated even after routine coronary artery bypass graft surgery and correlate with the duration of ischemia from AoXc.This process of CPB provides us with the ability to examine the transcriptional profile before and after an expected, consistent, and reproducible human ischemic event, albeit induced by cold cardioplegic arrest and not coronary occlusion.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: In addition, the absence of reperfusion in this time period allows us to examine the transcriptomic response to intermittent ischemia, without having to account for the perturbations of reperfusion injury.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Although various animal models have been used to examine the effects of ischemia on cardiac function, no human data exist which examine the early transcriptomic response to a left ventricular (LV) ischemic insult.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: We therefore characterized the effect of cold cardioplegia induced acute ischemia on the transcriptional profile of the LV by performing whole transcriptome next-generation RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) in patients undergoing cardiac surgery by sampling human LV tissue prior to, and after, the obligate ischemia during AoXC.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: We hypothesized that the cold cardioplegia induced ischemic injury will dramatically alter transcription in the human myocardium, and that we would identify genes and pathways, which will identify interventional targets for pharmacological therapy.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Methods:We have collected left ventricle tissue samples and blood sample from patients undergoing heart surgery.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: We obtained punch biopsies (~3-5μg total RNA content) from the site of a routinely placed surgical vent in the anterolateral apical left ventricular wall of patients undergoing elective aortic valve replacement surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: After an average of 79 minutes of aortic cross-clamping with intermittent cold blood cardioplegia for myocardial protection every 20 minutes, a second biopsy was obtained in the same manner.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Tissue samples were immediately placed in RNAlater® (Ambion, ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA), and after 48 hours at +4°C were stored at -80°C until RNA extraction.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Total RNA was isolated with Trizol and RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent, Santa Clara, CA).
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Libraries were prepared by poly(A) mRNA isolation and reverse transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR), then sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq2000 or HiSeq2500 (Illumina, San Diego, CA).
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: As samples were analyzed at different times, different read lengths were employed, initially using single-end reads (n=20) and then transitioning to paired end reads (n=216), ranging from 36 - 100 base pairs.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: Raw sequencing files were processed using Sickle, Skewer, and STAR software, and aligned to GrCh37 or UCSC Hg19.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: DNA was isolated from whole blood using standard methods.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: SNP genotyping was performed using the Illumina Omni2.5Exome-8 BeadChip array with additional exome content (Illumina, San Diego, CA) chip, version 1.1.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: We first phased and imputed 93 subjects using a phasing tool called SHAPEIT and an imputation tool called MINIMAC, with 1000 Genomes phase 1 version 3 for the reference panel.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: We then phased and imputed 26 more subjects using SHAPEIT, an imputation tool called IMPUTE2, and 1000 Genomes phase 3 version 5.
properties.title: TRanscriptomic ANalySis of left ventriCulaR gene Expression (TRANSCRibE)

properties.page_content: The Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP) was designed to evaluate whether continuous, long-term treatment (over a period of four to six years) with either an inhaled corticosteroid (budesonide) or an inhaled noncorticosteroid drug (nedocromil) safely produces an improvement in lung growth as compared with treatment for symptoms only (with albuterol and, if necessary, prednisone, administered as needed).

properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: BADGER is a 56-week randomized, double-blind, three-treatment, three-period cross-over trial that will evaluate the differential improvement in control that is achieved following three separate treatment interventions in children whose asthma is not acceptably controlled on a low dose of ICS (per NAEPP guidelines).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: All participants will enter an 8-week run-in period during which time they will receive a dose of 1x ICS (fluticasone 200 μg/day).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: During this 8-week time period, running 2-week averages to establish the lack of acceptable asthma control will be calculated.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: Thus, a child could qualify for randomization at any time during this 8-week run-in period.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: This approach should maximize both patient safety and successful enrollment.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: Children will continue to receive 1x ICS during the entire treatment phase.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: During each period of the treatment phase, they also will receive one add-on therapy in the form of LABA, LTRA or additional 1x ICS.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: The order of the add-on therapy assignment will be determined by randomization into one of six treatment sequences (order determined randomly).
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: Each treatment period will be 16 weeks in length; the initial 4 weeks of each period will be considered to be the washout period for the previous treatment.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome measures will be frequency of asthma exacerbations, asthma control days, and FEV1.
properties.title: NHLBI TOPMed: Best ADd-on Therapy Giving Effective Response (BADGER)

properties.page_content: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST).
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive condition characterized by narrowing or stiffening pulmonary arterioles resulting in increased pulmonary blood pressure and reduced delivery of oxygenated blood to the body.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: It is a common complication of sickle cell disease and initially presents with the symptom of shortness of breath (dyspnea) on exertion.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: As the condition worsens, other symptoms such as dizziness, lower extremity edema, and chest pain can develop.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: The drug, sildenafil, works by relaxing blood vessels in the lungs which reduces pulmonary blood pressure and allows more oxygenated blood to circulate.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Increased levels of oxygenated blood allows individuals with PAH to tolerate more activity, but guidelines for using sildenafil in patients with PAH and sickle cell disease were unavailable at the time of the Walk-PHaSST trial.Participants were screened for the existence of pulmonary hypertension with a six minute walk test and a Doppler echocardiogram that assessed TRV, diastolic function, and valvular and systolic function.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Subjects with TRV ≥ 2.7 m/s received further clinical evaluation for possible causes of pulmonary hypertension.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Other screening data included medical history, a physical exam, and standard laboratory testing.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: For individuals with moderate to severe pulmonary hypertension (TRV ≥ 3.0), a cardiac catheterization was done at the baseline and week 16 data collection periods.Subjects eligible for the main intervention trial based on screening results were randomized in a 1:1 double blind fashion to receive sildenafil or placebo for 16 weeks.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Subjects received 20 mg of oral sildenafil or matching placebo 3 times daily for 6 weeks, followed by 40 mg 3 times daily for 4 weeks, followed by 80 mg 3 times daily for 6 weeks, as tolerated.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Participants could also receive other therapies as needed to manage sickle cell and related complications.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome measure of the trial was change in the six minute walk test, a standard indicator of a person's heart and lung function and exercise capacity, from baseline to week 16.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: After completing the study treatment (or placebo), participants could choose to be part of the open-label follow-up phase of the study and continue to be assessed for up to one year.The study was intended to screen about 1000 subjects and randomize 132 subjects, however it was terminated early due to the unforeseen increase in adverse events in participants treated with sildenafil as compared to placebo.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: When the study was stopped, 33 participants had completed the trial.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: Subjects continued to be monitored, but were instructed to taper sildenafil treatment over three to seven days.There was no evidence that treatment with sildenafil impacted the six minute walk distance from baseline to week 16.
properties.title: Treatment of Pulmonary Hypertension and Sickle Cell Disease with Sildenafil Therapy (Walk-PHaSST)

properties.page_content: In addition, treatment with sildenafil appeared to increase rates of hospitalization due to sickle cell disease pain.Due to in part to the early termination of the trial, the majority of subject data was collected from the screening phase of the study (n=720), as opposed to the main intervention trial (n=74).Instructions for requesting individual-level data are available on BioData Catalyst at https://biodatacatalyst.nhlbi.nih.gov/resources/data/.

properties.title: Hematopoietic Cell Transplant for Sickle Cell Disease (HCT for SCD)

properties.title: Hematopoietic Cell Transplant for Sickle Cell Disease (HCT for SCD)

properties.title: Hematopoietic Cell Transplant for Sickle Cell Disease (HCT for SCD)

properties.page_content: Transplantation strategies have also evolved over time that has included transplant conditioning regimens of varying intensity, grafts other than bone marrow and novel approaches to overcome the donor-recipient histocompatibility barrier and limit graft-versus-host disease.

properties.page_content: To prevent first strokes, the Stroke Prevention Trial in Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP) used prophylactic transfusions in children who were identified by transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography as being at high risk for stroke.
properties.title: Optimizing Primary Stroke Prevention in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP II)

properties.page_content: This strategy reduced the incidence of stroke among such children from 10% per year to less than 1% per year, leading to recommendations for TCD screening and prophylactic transfusion for children with abnormal velocities on ultrasonography.
properties.title: Optimizing Primary Stroke Prevention in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP II)

properties.page_content: Despite the reduced risk of stroke, long-term use of transfusions can cause adverse side effects, such as iron overload or alloimmunization.
properties.title: Optimizing Primary Stroke Prevention in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP II)

properties.page_content: However, cessation of transfusions is associated with recurrence of stroke, and at the time of the STOP II trial, there were no clinical or laboratory indicators to guide the duration of prophylaxis.
properties.title: Optimizing Primary Stroke Prevention in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP II)

properties.page_content: Therefore the STOP II trial was initiated to determine whether transfusions could be limited by monitoring patients with TCD examinations after transfusions were halted and resuming transfusions if the examination indicated a high risk of stroke.The trial was halted for safety concerns after 79 of a planned 100 children were randomized.
properties.title: Optimizing Primary Stroke Prevention in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (STOP II)

properties.page_content: Discontinuation of transfusion for the prevention of stroke in children with sickle cell disease resulted in a high rate of reversion to abnormal blood-flow velocities on Doppler studies and stroke incidence.Instructions for requesting individual-level data are available on BioData Catalyst at https://biodatacatalyst.nhlbi.nih.gov/resources/data/.

properties.page_content: Sickle cell anemia is associated with substantial morbidity from acute complications and organ dysfunction beginning in the first year of life.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: In 1995, the Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea (MSH) (dbGaP phs002348) demonstrated that, in adults, hydroxyurea is effective in decreasing the frequency of painful crises, hospitalizations for crises, acute chest syndrome, and blood transfusions by 50%.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: The phase I/II study of hydroxyurea in children (HUG KIDS) demonstrated that children have a response to hydroxyurea similar to that seen in adults in terms of increasing fetal hemoglobin levels and total hemoglobin, and decreasing complications associated with sickle cell anemia.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: In addition, this study demonstrated that the drug does not adversely affect growth and development between the ages of 5 and 15.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: A pilot study of hydroxyurea (HUSOFT) given to children between the ages of 6 months and 24 months demonstrated that the drug was well tolerated and that the fetal hemoglobin levels rose and remained elevated compared to baseline with continued hydroxyurea administration.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: A Special Emphasis Panel (SEP) met on April 12, 1996 to review the results of the MSH trial and the progress to date of the HUG KIDS study.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: The SEP recommended that NHLBI undertake the BABY HUG trial.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: The BABY HUG Randomized Controlled Trial concluded that hydroxyurea treatment in very young children seemed to have an acceptable safety profile and to reduce complications of sickle cell anemia.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: However, more data were needed on the long-term safety of hydroxyurea use in very young children.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: As a result, follow-up studies were initiated.
properties.title: Hydroxyurea to Prevent Organ Damage in Children with Sickle Cell Anemia (BABY HUG) Phase III Clinical Trial and Follow-Up Observational Studies I and II

properties.page_content: The Follow-Up Study II provided longer follow-up than Follow-Up Study I, and included more assessment types than Follow-Up Study I.The BABY HUG program consisted of three related studies, each of which has associated datasets and bio-specimens.

properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: The sample was selected by identifying affected probands who had laboratory diagnosed obstructive sleep apnea.
properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: In addition, during the first 5 study years, neighborhood control families were identified through a neighborhood proband, and his/her spouses and first-degree relatives.
properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: For the first three visits, data, including an overnight sleep study, were collected in participants' homes while the last visit occurred in a general clinical research center (GCRC).
properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.title: National Sleep Research Resource (NSRR): Cleveland Family Study (CFS)

properties.page_content: Cohort DescriptionIn 1948, the researchers recruited 5,209 men and women between the ages of 30 and 62 from the town of Framingham, Massachusetts, and began the first round of extensive physical examinations and lifestyle interviews that they would later analyze for common patterns related to CVD development.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: Since 1948, the subjects have returned to the study every two years for an examination consisting of a detailed medical history, physical examination, and laboratory tests, and in 1971, the study enrolled a second-generation cohort -- 5,124 of the original participants' adult children and their spouses -- to participate in similar examinations.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: The second examination of the Offspring cohort occurred eight years after the first examination, and subsequent examinations have occurred approximately every four years thereafter.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: In 1994, the need to establish a new study reflecting a more diverse community of Framingham was recognized, and the first Omni cohort of the Framingham Heart Study, consisting of 506 participants, was enrolled.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: In April 2002 4095 third generation of participants, the grandchildren of the original cohort, were added.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: In 2003, 103 spouses of the offspring Cohort (NOS), and a second group of 410 Omni participants were enrolled.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.page_content: Through 2019, the original cohort has completed a total of 32 exams, the Offspring cohort 9 exams, the OMNI1 cohort 4 exams, and GEN3, NOS and OMNI2 cohorts each have completed 3 exams.
properties.title: Collaborative Cohort of Cohorts for COVID-19 Research (C4R): Framingham Heart Study (FHS)

properties.title: A Pilot Trial of Complement Inhibition Using Eculizumab to Overcome Platelet Transfusion Refractoriness in HLA Allo-Immunized Patients

properties.page_content: Platelet transfusion can be a life-saving procedure in preventing or treating serious bleeding in patients who have low and/or dysfunctional platelets.
properties.title: A Pilot Trial of Complement Inhibition Using Eculizumab to Overcome Platelet Transfusion Refractoriness in HLA Allo-Immunized Patients

properties.page_content: Heavily transfused patients frequently develop human leukocyte antigen (HLA) allo-immunization resulting in platelet transfusion refractoriness and a high risk for life-threatening thrombocytopenia.
properties.title: A Pilot Trial of Complement Inhibition Using Eculizumab to Overcome Platelet Transfusion Refractoriness in HLA Allo-Immunized Patients

properties.page_content: Data suggest complement activation leading to the destruction of platelets bound by HLA allo-antibodies may play a pathophysiologic role in platelet refractoriness.
properties.title: A Pilot Trial of Complement Inhibition Using Eculizumab to Overcome Platelet Transfusion Refractoriness in HLA Allo-Immunized Patients

properties.page_content: We conducted a pilot trial to investigate the use of eculizumab to treat platelet transfusion refractoriness in allo-immunized patients with severe thrombocytopenia.
properties.title: A Pilot Trial of Complement Inhibition Using Eculizumab to Overcome Platelet Transfusion Refractoriness in HLA Allo-Immunized Patients

properties.page_content: We hypothesized that when we treated patients having platelet refractoriness with eculizumab, platelet counts would increase to higher numbers after platelet transfusions, decreasing the risk of bleeding complications associated with having a low platelet count.
