properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.page_content: In this study, 310 psoriasis patients from The Psoriasis, Atherosclerosis, and Cardiometabolic Disease Initiative (PACI) were studied at baseline to determine if levels of circulating apolipoprotein A-1 predict early onset coronary artery disease in inflammatory conditions.
properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis
entities: The Psoriasis, Atherosclerosis, and Cardiometabolic Disease Initiative

properties.page_content: Of the 310 participants, 124 were followed for four years to determine if apolipoprotein A-1 predicts non-calcified coronary burden over time.
properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.page_content: The primary outcome of this study was non-calcified coronary burden by coronary computed tomography angiography.
properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.page_content: For ApoA-1 quantification, fasting blood draw was performed the same day as the coronary computed tomography angiography.
properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.title: ApoA-1 and Atherosclerosis in Psoriasis

properties.page_content: The NIH Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER) initiative comprises a set of three combined retrospective and prospective, longitudinal and observational meta-cohort studies with nested case-control studies designed to define and characterize the epidemiology, natural history, clinical spectrum, and underlying mechanisms of post-acute effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC or Post-COVID syndrome) in a diverse study population representative of the general COVID-19 population in the US.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: Enrolled patients, with and without known SARS-CoV-2 infection, will be observed for clinical signs and symptoms of PASC and will be assessed for risk and resiliency factors and potential mediating factors associated with the severity and progression of PASC.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The objective of the RECOVER initiative is to enhance knowledge of recovery from SARS-CoV-2 infections in order to support development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: Overarching scientific objectives are as follows:Characterize the incidence and prevalence of sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.Characterize the spectrum of clinical symptoms, subclinical organ dysfunction, natural history, and distinct phenotypes identified as sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: Define the biological mechanisms underlying pathogenesis of the sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The RECOVER observational studies comprise three cohorts across the lifespan (adult, pediatric, and tissue pathology (autopsy)).
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The data collection and data analysis plans for each cohort have been harmonized to use common data elements where feasible.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: Individuals with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection, and with or without PASC symptoms, will be followed to identify risk factors and occurrence of PASC.

properties.page_content: 3) NIH RECOVER: A Multi-site Pathology Study of Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection The RECOVER tissue pathology study is a cross-sectional study designed to define and characterize the epidemiology, natural history, clinical spectrum, and underlying mechanisms of post-acute effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection in a diverse population representative of the general COVID-19 population in the US.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The autopsy study will characterize the pathology of PASC in (i) non-hospitalized patients who die 30 days or later from symptom onset of COVID-19, and (ii) hospitalized patients who die 30 days or later after discharge from a hospitalization for COVID-19.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The study will include decedents who had previously fully recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection (i.e., >30 days from onset in non-hospitalized, or >30 days from discharge in hospitalized patients), and decedents who meet clinical criteria of PASC as defined by the recent World Health Organization publication (see Section 5.4 below).
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The autopsy study will also explore the pathology of acute SARS-CoV-2 infection in a smaller subset of patients who died 15-30 days from symptom onset.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: This protocol defines the common set of clinical data elements, autopsy procedures for tissue collection, core measures, pathology protocols, shared pathology tissues, data elements, and methodology.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: Each investigator site is expected to perform autopsies on the decedents to address the pathophysiology of the potential long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on human health.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.page_content: The Consortium analysis plan aims to address research questions by incorporating: 1) tissue obtained from autopsies performed at each Phase II participant's site; and 2) tissue available from other pathology investigators/autopsy sites within the Consortium.
properties.title: NIH RECOVER-Pediatric: Understanding the Long-Term Impact of COVID on Children and Families

properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ObjectivesThe primary objective is to determine event-free survival (EFS) at 1 year after unrelated donor (URD) hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) using bone marrow (BM) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD).BackgroundSickle cell disease (SCD), also known as sickle cell anemia, is an inherited blood disease that can cause organ damage, stroke, and intense pain episodes.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Children with sickle cell disease experience organ damage, impaired quality of life, and premature mortality.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A blood stem cell transplant is a treatment option for someone with a severe form of the disease.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Prior to undergoing a transplant, people typically receive a conditioning regimen of high doses of chemotherapy and other medications to prepare the body to accept the transplant.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: This type of conditioning regimen is known as a myeloablative conditioning regimen, but it can result in toxicities and sterility.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A conditioning regimen that uses lower doses of chemotherapy and medications may be safer for transplant recipients.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: This type of regimen is known as reduced intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: RIC has a more favorable toxicity profile but is associated with higher rates of graft rejection (GR), especially with graft sources such as umbilical cord blood This study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of blood stem cell transplants, using bone marrow from unrelated donors, in children with severe SCD who receive a RIC regimen prior to the transplant.SubjectsPatients 3.0-19.75 years old with symptomatic SCD AND one or more of the following complications: (1)-(i) a clinically significant neurologic event (stroke) or any neurologic defect lasting > 24 hours and accompanied by an infarct on cerebral magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); OR, (ii) patients who have a Transcranial Doppler (TCD) velocity that exceeds 200 cm/sec by the non-imaging technique (or TCD measurement of >185 cm/sec by the imaging technique) measured at a minimum of 2 separate occasions one month or more apart; OR, (2) Minimum of two episodes of acute chest syndrome within the preceding 2-year period defined as new pulmonary alveolar consolidation involving at least one complete lung segment (associated with acute symptoms including fever, chest pain, tachypnea, wheezing, rales, or cough that is not attributed to asthma or bronchiolitis) despite adequate supportive care measures; OR, (3) History of 3 or more severe pain events (defined as new onset of pain that lasts for at least 2 hours for which there is no other explanation) per year in the 2 years prior to enrollment despite adequate supportive care measures (if patients are receiving hydroxyurea and compliant with therapy, being symptomatic is an indication for transplantation; however, if patients decline hydroxyurea or non-compliant with this therapy, they would still remain eligible for study if pain criteria as described above are met).
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Lansky/Karnofsky performance score must be ≥ 40.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Hemoglobin S must be ≤ 45%.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Patients must have an unrelated adult bone marrow donor who is HLA-matched at 8 of 8 HLA-A, -B, -C and -DRB1 at high resolution using DNA-based typing.
properties.title: Unrelated Donor Reduced Intensity Bone Marrow Transplant for Children with Severe Sickle Cell Disease (BMT CTN-0601-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Available DataThe available data include all elements of the previously released SPRINT Primary Outcome Paper (SPRINT-POP) data, the full SPRINT clinical data including the MRI and MIND data, and select ancillary study data (Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring, APOL1, Acute Kidney Injury, ASK, Heart, FAST, PWV, Renal Resistance, Biomarkers, Plasma AD).ObjectiveThe Systolic Blood Pressure Trial (SPRINT) was conducted to test the hypothesis that treating systolic blood pressure to a target of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared to a target of less than 140 mm Hg, would reduce the incidence of cardiovascular disease.BackgroundHypertension is a highly prevalent condition among adults and is a leading risk factor for myocardial infarction and stroke.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Further, isolated systolic hypertension is the most common form of hypertension in adults over 50 years of age.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Observational studies have shown a monotonic increase in cardiovascular risk with systolic blood pressures above 115 mm Hg; however, general population clinical trials have only documented the benefits of lowering systolic blood pressure to a target of 150 mm Hg.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A 2007 expert panel sponsored by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute designated the hypothesis that lowering the systolic blood pressure goal to a level <120 mm Hg as the most important hypothesis to test in reducing hypertension related complications in those without diabetes.SubjectsA total of 9361 participants were enrolled, with 4,678 randomized to the intensive-treatment group and 4,683 randomized to the standard-treatment group.DesignSPRINT was a randomized, single blinded (outcome adjudicators were blinded to treatment assignment) treatment trial with participants randomized to a systolic blood-pressure target of either less than 140 mm Hg (the standard-treatment group) or less than 120 mm Hg (the intensive-treatment group).
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)
entities: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

properties.page_content: Following randomization, baseline hypertensive regimens were adjusted in accordance with study treatment algorithms established for each group.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The study formulary included all major classes of antihypertensive agents.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Investigators could prescribe other antihypertensive medications, but the use of drug classes with the strongest evidence for reduction in cardiovascular outcomes was encouraged.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: This included thiazide-type diuretics as the first-line agent, loop diuretics for participants with advanced chronic kidney disease, and beta-adrenergic blockers for participants with coronary artery disease.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Medications for participants in the intensive-treatment group were adjusted on a monthly basis to target a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Medications for participants in the standard-treatment group were adjusted to target a systolic blood pressure of 135 to 139 mm Hg, and the dose was reduced if systolic blood pressure was less than 130 mm Hg on a single visit or less than 135 mm Hg on two consecutive visits.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Lifestyle modification was encouraged as part of the management strategy.Participants were seen monthly for the first 3 months and every 3 months thereafter.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Demographic data were collected at baseline.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Clinical and laboratory data were obtained at baseline and every 3 months thereafter.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A structured interview was used in both groups every 3 months to obtain self-reported cardiovascular disease outcomes.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Medical records and electrocardiograms were obtained for documentation of events.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Incidences of hypotension, syncope, injurious falls, electrolyte abnormalities, and bradycardia that were evaluated in an emergency department were included in adverse event reporting.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Occurrences of acute kidney injury or acute renal failure requiring hospitalization were also monitored.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome was a composite outcome of myocardial infarction, other acute coronary syndromes, stroke, heart failure, or death from cardiovascular causes.ConclusionsThe blood pressure intervention was stopped in August of 2015 (median follow-up of 3.26 years) after the cardiovascular outcome results exceeded the boundary for efficacy at two consecutive time points.
properties.title: Systolic Blood Pressure Intervention Trial (SPRINT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Compared with a systolic blood pressure target of less than 140 mm Hg, an intensive systolic blood pressure target of 120 mm Hg resulted in lower rates of fatal and nonfatal major cardiovascular events and death from any cause.

properties.page_content: Significantly higher rates of some adverse events were observed in the intensive-treatment group.

properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Objectives To test whether therapy with a GLP-1 agonist improves clinical stability following hospitalization for acute heart failure.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Background Heart failure was the leading cause of hospitalization in the United States with more than 4 million admissions per year from 2003–2009.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Abnormal cardiac metabolism contributes to the pathophysiology of advanced heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: As heart failure progresses, these abnormalities become more pronounced and are observed in both patients with and without type 2 diabetes.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: At this time of this study, there was no heart failure therapy that targeted these metabolic abnormalities; however, in earlier clinical studies, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) agonists showed cardioprotective effects in patients with advanced heart failure, irrespective of type 2 diabetes status.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Glucagon-like peptide 1 is an endogenous incretin hormone that improves insulin sensitivity with minimal risk of hypoglycemia.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: This study was created to determine if use of GLP-1 agonists improved clinical stability in recently hospitalized patients with acute heart failure and reduced LVEF.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants There were 300 participants. Design Participants were identified by hospital admission records and were enrolled during either the last 24 hours of his or her hospitalization for heart failure or the 2-week interval after the hospitalization.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Baseline evaluations were conducted, which included echocardiographic measures, the 6-minute walk test, the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), and blood tests.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: After the baseline evaluation, patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either the GLP-1 agonist liraglutide or placebo as a daily subcutaneous injection.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The protocol involved titration of study drug dosage as tolerated every 14 days from 0.6 mg/d to 1.2 mg/d to 1.8 mg/d during the first 30 days of the trial (as tolerated).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Follow-up testing was performed at 30-, 90-, and 180-day study visits.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary end point was a global rank score in which all participants, regardless of treatment assignment, were ranked across 3 hierarchical tiers: time to death, time to rehospitalization for heart failure, and time-averaged proportional change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) level from baseline to 180 days.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Conclusions The GLP-1 agonist liraglutide did not improve post-hospitalization clinical stability in patients with advanced heart failure and reduced LVEF.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: There was no significant between-group difference in the global rank scores and furthermore, there were no significant differences detected in any of the secondary endpoints.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Functional Impact of GLP-1 for Heart Failure Treatment (HFN FIGHT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Data Access NOTE: Please refer to the "Authorized Access" section below for information about how access to the data from this accession differs from many other dbGaP accessions.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Related StudiesEcho images are available with HFN-NEAT Imaging.ObjectivesTo determine the effect of isosorbide mononitrate on daily activity in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction.Background Nitrates are commonly prescribed for symptom relief in patients with heart failure.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Early studies in patients with heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction concluded that long-acting nitrates improve activity tolerance; however, approximately half of heart failure patients have preserved ejection fraction.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The effects of nitrates in patients with heart failure and a preserved ejection fraction have not been extensively studied and the overall effect of nitrates on activity tolerance in such patients is uncertain.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ParticipantsThere were a total of 110 participants enrolled with 51 participants assigned to receive isosorbide mono-nitrate first and placebo second, and 59 participants assigned to receive placebo first and isosorbide mononitrate second.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Design Enrolled participants underwent baseline assessments, including echocardiography, quality-of-life scores, 6-minute walk test distance, and NT-proBNP levels.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: participants were also supplied with two kinetic activity monitors containing high-sensitivity triaxis accelerometers, to be worn 24 hours per day.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The accelerometer measurements were expressed as arbitrary accelerometer units and stored every 15 minutes equaling 96 data points per day.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The 15-minute cumulative accelerometer units were totaled over a 24-hour period to provide daily accelerometer units.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants were assigned to one of two treatment groups: 6 weeks of placebo first with crossover to 6 weeks of isosorbide mononitrate, or 6 weeks of isosorbide mononitrate first with crossover to 6 weeks of placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The study drugs were prepared as 30-mg tablets of isosorbide mononitrate and matching placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: During each 6-week period, participants were instructed to take no study drug for the first 2 weeks followed by one tablet (30 mg daily) for 1 week, two tablets (60 mg once daily) for 1 week, and four tablets (120 mg once daily) until the next study visit, for a treatment duration of at least 2 weeks and up to 4 weeks.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: After each 6-week period, participants returned to the study center to repeat end-point assessments.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome for the study was the comparison of average daily accelerometer units during the period in which participants were receiving the 120-mg dose of isosorbide mononitrate compared to the period in which participants received the placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Other secondary end points included the 6-minute walk distance and the post-walk Borg dyspnea score, scores on the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire and the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire, and NT-proBNP levels.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)
entities: Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire
keyphrases: Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire

properties.page_content: In addition, participants completed a questionnaire indicating in which period (first, second, no preference) they felt better.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Conclusions Participants were active for fewer hours of the day during the 120-mg phase of receipt of isosorbide mononitrate as compared with placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Furthermore, during all study-drug regimens combined (30 mg to 120 mg), participants were less active during receipt of isosorbide mononitrate as compared with placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: There was no significant effect of isosorbide mononitrate on secondary outcomes.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Nitrate's Effect on Activity Tolerance in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFN NEAT-BioLINCC)

entities: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes

properties.page_content: Related StudiesWhole genome and whole exome data is available on a subset of participants with phs001411.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ECG signal data is available with phs003562.ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to determine if intensive glycemic control, multiple lipid management and intensive blood pressure control could prevent major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke or cardiovascular death) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Secondary hypotheses included treatment differences in other cardiovascular outcomes, total mortality, microvascular outcomes, health-related quality of life and cost-effectiveness.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: BackgroundGlycemia Trial:Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus die of cardiovascular disease (CVD) at rates two to four times higher than non-diabetic populations of similar demographic characteristics.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: They also experience increased rates of nonfatal myocardial infarction and stroke.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: With the growing prevalence of obesity in the United States, CVD associated with type 2 diabetes is expected to become an even greater public health challenge in the coming decades than it is now.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Expected increases in event rates will be associated with a concomitant rise in suffering and resource utilization.The ACCORD study investigated whether intensive therapy to target normal glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels would reduce cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes who had either established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors when compared to standard therapy (HbA1c between 7.0% and 7.9%).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A separate analysis investigated whether reduction of blood glucose concentration decreases the rate of microvascular complications in these patients.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Lipid Therapy Trial: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus have an increased incidence of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease attributable, in part, to associated risk factors such as dyslipidemia.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: This is characterized by elevated plasma triglyceride levels, low levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and small, dense low-density lipoprotein (LDL) particles.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The ACCORD Lipid Therapy trial was designed to test the effect of a therapeutic strategy that uses a fibrate to raise HDL-C and lower triglyceride levels and uses a statin for treatment of LDL-C reduce the rate of CVD events compared to a strategy that only uses a statin for treatment of LDL-C on cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes that were at high risk for cardiovascular disease.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Blood Pressure Trial: Diabetes mellitus increases the risk of cardiovascular disease at every level of systolic blood pressure.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Because cardiovascular risk in patients with diabetes is graded and continuous across the entire range of levels of systolic blood pressure, even at prehypertensive levels, the Seventh Report of the Joint National Committee on Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Treatment of High Blood Pressure (JNC 7) recommended beginning drug treatment in patients with diabetes who have systolic blood pressures of 130 mm Hg or higher, with a treatment goal of reducing systolic blood pressure to below 130 mm Hg.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)
entities: Joint National Committee on Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Treatment of High Blood Pressure

properties.page_content: There is, however, a paucity of evidence from randomized clinical trials to support these recommendations.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The ACCORD Blood Pressure trial tested the effect of a target systolic blood pressure below 120 mm Hg on major cardiovascular events among high-risk persons with type 2 diabetes compared to a strategy that targeted a SBP of < 140 mm Hg.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: EYE Substudy: Diabetic retinopathy, an important microvascular complication of diabetes, is a leading cause of blindness in the United States.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Randomized, controlled clinical trials in cohorts of patients with type 1 diabetes and those with type 2 diabetes have shown the beneficial effects of intensive glycemic control and intensive treatment of elevated blood pressure on the progression of diabetic retinopathy.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Elevated serum cholesterol and triglyceride levels have been implicated, in observational studies and small trials, as additional risk factors for the development of diabetic retinopathy and visual loss.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The ACCORD EYE Substudy evaluated the effects of the ACCORD medical strategies on the progression of diabetic retinopathy in a subgroup of trial patients.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)
keyphrases: effects of the ACCORD medical strategies

properties.page_content: MIND Substudy: Studies suggest that older persons with type 2 diabetes have at least twice the likelihood of developing late-life cognitive impairment or dementia compared to those without.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The mechanisms underlying these cognitive disorders are increasingly thought to reflect a mixed pathology pattern with contributions from vascular, neurodegenerative and neurovascular processes.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Pathophysiological mechanisms that have been described include inflammation, oxidative stress, energy imbalance, protein misfolding, glucocorticoid-mediated effects and differences in genetic susceptibilities.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The ACCORD MIND substudy took as a premise that early intervention with the ACCORD therapeutic strategies to improve glycemic control could mitigate the adverse effects of type 2 diabetes on the brain.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants10,251 participants with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c concentrations of 7.5% or more participated in the trial.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Of these patients, 5518 were assigned to the lipid therapy arm and 4733 to the blood pressure arm.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: EYE Substudy: A subgroup of 2856 participants was evaluated for the effects of the ACCORD interventions at 4 years on the progression of diabetic retinopathy.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants who, at baseline, had a history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy that had been treated with laser photocoagulation or vitrectomy were excluded.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: MIND Substudy: A subgroup of 2977 participants was evaluated for cognitive function and brain volume.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The ACCORD MIND substudy excluded participants aged <55 years and those in the Veteran's Administration CCN (to retain the overall sex balance reflected in the other CCNs).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Within ACCORD MIND a group of 632 participants participated in the MRI sub-study.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Design Participants were randomly assigned to undergo either intensive glycemic control (targeting a glycated hemoglobin level <6.0%) or standard therapy (targeting a glycated hemoglobin level of 7.0 to 7.9%).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Of these participants, 5518 with dyslipidemia were also randomly assigned, in a 2-by-2 factorial design, to receive simvastatin (to reduce low-density lipoprotein [LDL] cholesterol levels) in combination with either fenofibrate (to reduce triglyceride levels and increase high-density lipoprotein [HDL] cholesterol levels) or matching placebo.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The remaining 4733 participants were randomly assigned, in a 2-by-2 factorial design, to undergo either intensive blood-pressure control (targeting a systolic blood pressure <120 mm Hg) or standard therapy (targeting a systolic blood pressure <140 mm Hg).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke or death from cardiovascular causes.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Clinic staff and participants were not blinded to treatment arm.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The finding of higher mortality in the intensive-therapy group led to a discontinuation of intensive therapy after a mean of 3.5 years of follow-up.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Analysis was done for all participants who were assessed for microvascular outcomes, on the basis of treatment assignment, irrespective of treatments received or compliance to therapies.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: EYE Substudy: EYE Substudy participants were evaluated at two standardized and comprehensive eye examinations for the effects of the ACCORD interventions at 4 years on the progression of diabetic retinopathy by 3 or more steps on the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Severity Scale (as assessed from seven-field stereoscopic fundus photographs, with 17 possible steps and a higher number of steps indicating greater severity) or the development of diabetic retinopathy necessitating laser photocoagulation or vitrectomy.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)
entities: Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Severity Scale
keyphrases: Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study Severity Scale

properties.page_content: MIND Substudy: The cognitive primary outcome, the Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) score, was assessed at baseline, 20 and 40 months.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Total brain volume (TBV), the primary brain structure outcome, was assessed with MRI at baseline and 40 months in a sub-set of 632 patients.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: All patients with follow-up data were included in the primary analyses.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Conclusions Glycemia Trial: As compared with standard therapy, the use of intensive therapy to target normal glycated hemoglobin levels for 3.5 years increased mortality and did not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: (Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Study Group, et al.,2008, PMID:18539917).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)
entities: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Study Group

properties.page_content: Microvascular Outcomes of the Glycemia Trial: Intensive therapy did not reduce the risk of advanced measures of microvascular outcomes, but delayed the onset of albuminuria and some measures of eye complications and neuropathy.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Microvascular benefits of intensive therapy should be weighed against the risk of increased total and cardiovascular disease-related mortality, increased weight gain, and higher risk for severe hypoglycemia.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: (Ismail-Beigi et al., 2010, PMID: 20594588) Lipid Therapy Trial: The combination of fenofibrate and simvastatin did not reduce the rate of fatal cardiovascular events, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke, as compared with simvastatin alone.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: These results do not support the routine use of combination therapy with fenofibrate and simvastatin to reduce cardiovascular risk in the majority of high-risk patients with type 2 diabetes (ACCORD Study Group, et al., 2010, PMID: 20228404).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Blood Pressure Trial: In patients with type 2 diabetes at high risk for cardiovascular events, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the rate of a composite outcome of fatal and nonfatal major cardiovascular events (ACCORD Study Group, et al., 2010, PMID: 20228401).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: EYE Substudy: Intensive glycemic control and intensive combination treatment of dyslipidemia, but not intensive blood-pressure control, reduced the rate of progression of diabetic retinopathy (ACCORD Study Group, et al., 2010, PMID: 20587587).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: MIND Substudy: Although significant differences in TBV favored the intensive therapy, cognitive outcomes were not different.
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Combined with the unfavorable effects on other ACCORD outcomes, MIND findings do not support using intensive therapy to reduce the adverse effects of diabetes on the brain in patients similar to MIND patients (Launer et al., 2011, PMID: 21958949).
properties.title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD-BioLINCC)

properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ObjectivesTo test the hypothesis that, compared to placebo, oral iron repletion in heart failure patients with iron deficiency improves exercise capacity after 16 weeks of therapy.Background Iron deficiency affects approximately one half of patients with symptomatic heart failure.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The presence of iron deficiency in patients with heart failure is associated with reduced functional capacity, poorer quality of life, and increased mortality.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Despite growing recognition of the significance of iron deficiency, randomized multicenter trials exploring the utility of oral iron supplementation, a therapy that is inexpensive, readily available, and safe, have not been performed in patients with heart failure.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Moreover, patient characteristics and biochemical profiles that may influence responsiveness to oral iron in patients with heart failure have not been defined.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Results of intravenous iron repletion trials have been favorable, but regularly treating patients with intravenous iron products is expensive and poses logistical challenges for outpatients.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Therefore, the HFN-IRONOUT study was initiated to investigate the efficacy of oral iron in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ParticipantsA total of 225 participants were enrolled, 111 randomized to receive oral iron and 114 randomized to receive the placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Design The HFN-IRONOUT study was a phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial that enrolled participants at 23 sites in the United States.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants were randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, to receive either oral iron polysaccharide or placebo with the use of an automated web-based system.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A permuted block randomization method (with 4 participants per block) was stratified by enrolling site and anemia status (defined as hemoglobin < 12 g/dL).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Study drug was administered orally at 150 mg, twice daily for 16 weeks.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: At baseline, 8 weeks, and 16 weeks participants underwent studies including history and physical examination, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ), and 6-minute walk test.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: CPETs were performed using a 10 Watt/minute incremental ramp protocol and breath-by-breath measures of oxygen uptake were uniformly analyzed by the CPET Core Lab.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants also underwent phlebotomy for biomarkers.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Iron studies, including iron, total iron binding capacity, and ferritin, were measured at baseline and after 16 weeks to determine the extent to which oral iron led to iron repletion.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary end point was the change in peak oxygen uptake (peak VO2) after 16 weeks of therapy.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Conclusions Among participants with HFrEF with iron deficiency, high-dose oral iron did not improve exercise capacity over 16 weeks.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network Oral Iron Repletion Effects on Oxygen Uptake in Heart Failure (HFN IRONOUT-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE).
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: Leveraging access to the blood supply and blood donors, the REDS-IV-P program began conducting the RESPONSE study (REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic) in early 2020 in order to 1) evaluate if SARS-CoV-2 RNA was found in blood donations in the U.S.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: using an assay that could potentially be used to screen the blood supply if evidence of SARS-CoV-2 transfusion-transmission became apparent 2) conduct serosurveys using optimized assays/algorithms to monitor antibody reactivity in blood donor populations over time, 3) enroll SARS-CoV-2 positive donors and others into a longitudinal cohort study to answer fundamental questions about the evolution of viremia and immune responses, and 4) establish a sharable biorepository that includes specimens collected early on in the infection and potentially large volumes of plasma from infected/convalescent donors.Screening for SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia was completed using a SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid test (NAT) performed on retained blood donor minipool samples from six geographic regions in the US.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: The study also included serosurveillance (i.e.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: testing for antibody directed against the SARS-CoV2 spike protein) of donations from the same six regions to document accruing seroincidence in blood donor populations and to project these rates in the general population.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: To enrich for donors with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, another part of the study focused on donors reporting post-donation information (PDI) consistent with COVID-19 by testing plasma from all available PDI donations for SARS-CoV-2 RNA by NAT.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: Subjects who were diagnosed with COVID-19 based on PDI reports or who tested positive by SARS-CoV-2 NAT on index donation plasma were enrolled into a longitudinal follow-up study which collected multiple samples for up to one-year post-infection.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: The longitudinal follow-up study also enrolled community members who reported a new positive SARS-CoV-2 NAT test in the prior 7-14 days.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: The specific aims of the RESPONSE study were to:  Establish the incidence of SARS-CoV-2 RNAemia in blood donations from the American Red Cross (ARC) regions in Los Angeles, Boston, and Minneapolis metropolitan areas, Bloodworks Northwest (BWNW), New York Blood Center (NYBC), and Vitalant San Francisco Bay Area, monthly between March and September of 2020  Conduct serosurveys to study antibody reactivity in same six areas as above monthly for March to August 2020  Document rates of Post Donation Information (PDI) reports to determine PDI rates relevant to SARS-CoV-2 clinical disease and test index donation plasma from PDI donors for SARS-CoV-2 RNA Enroll SARS-CoV-2 infected subjects into a longitudinal cohort study to answer fundamental questions on the evolution of viremia, early immune responses and waning of immunity over 3-12 months of follow-up  Establish a sharable biorepository of samples from all of the above Aims for future research   The data from Aims 3 and 4 above is being made available in BioData Catalyst.Biospecimens for these Aims are managed by Vitalant Research Institute (VRI).
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: More information on biospecimens is available.
properties.title: REDS-IV-P Epidemiology, Surveillance and Preparedness of the Novel SARS-CoV-2 Epidemic (RESPONSE)

properties.page_content: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ObjectivesTo test the two independent hypotheses that when compared to placebo, addition of: (1) low dose dopamine; or (2) low dose nesiritide to diuretic therapy will enhance decongestion and preserve renal function in patients with acute heart failure and renal dysfunction.Background A primary treatment goal in acute heart failure is to achieve adequate decongestion while avoiding renal dysfunction and other side effects.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Patients with acute heart failure and moderate or severe renal dysfunction are at risk for inadequate decongestion and worsening renal function - both of which are associated with worse outcomes.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Renal adjuvant therapies that enhance decongestion and preserve renal function during treatment of acute heart failure are needed.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Dopamine is an endogenous catecholamine which, at low doses, may selectively activate dopamine receptors and promote renal vasodilatation.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Previous studies have suggested that the addition of low dose dopamine to diuretic therapy enhances decongestion and preserves renal function during diuretic therapy in acute heart failure; however, these studies were small with variable study designs and dopamine doses.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is a cardiac peptide with vasodilating, renin and aldosterone inhibiting, natriuretic and diuretic properties.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Nesiritide is human recombinant BNP approved for management of acute heart failure.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The recommended dose lowers blood pressure and atrial pressures and produces modest improvement in dyspnea, but does not favorably impact clinical outcomes or renal function, potentially due to its hypotensive effects.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Small studies using low dose nesiritide in acute heart failure and cardiac surgery patients have demonstrated favorable effects on urine output and renal function.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Therefore, the Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation (ROSE) trial was initiated to determine the benefits and safety of intravenous administration of low dose nesiritide or low dose dopamine in patients with congestive heart failure and kidney dysfunction.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: ParticipantsA total of 360 participants were enrolled.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Design Participants were enrolled within 24 hours of hospital admission and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to the nesiritide or dopamine strategies.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants randomized to the dopamine strategy were randomized in a double-blind 2:1 ratio to low dose dopamine (2 µg/kg/min for 72 hours infused via local guideline stipulated vascular access) or placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants randomized to the nesiritide strategy were randomized in a double-blind 2:1 ratio to low dose nesiritide (0.005 μg/kg/min for 72 hours infused via peripheral intravenous access without initial bolus) or placebo.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: All participants received open-label, intravenous loop diuretic treatment with a recommended total daily dose equal to 2.5x the total daily oral outpatient furosemide (or equivalent) dose at 7 days prior to admission up to a maximum of 600 mg/day.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants naive to outpatient loop diuretics received 80 mg/day of intravenous furosemide.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: One-half of the total daily diuretic dose was administered as a bolus twice daily for at least 24 hours.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Use of other medications and diuretic dosing after 24 hours were at the discretion of the clinician.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: All participants were placed on a 2000 mg sodium diet and 2000 cc fluid restriction.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: After the primary endpoint assessment at 72 hours, study drug was discontinued and subsequent treatment was at the clinician's discretion.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The two co-primary endpoints were the 72-hour cumulative urinary volume as an index of decongestion efficacy and the change in cystatin-C from randomization to 72 hours as a measure of renal function preservation.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Conclusions In participants with acute heart failure and renal dysfunction, neither low-dose dopamine nor low-dose nesiritide enhanced decongestion or improved renal function when added to diuretic therapy.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network - Renal Optimization Strategies Evaluation in Acute Heart Failure and Reliable Evaluation of Dyspnea (HFN ROSE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The Framingham Heart Study (FHS) is a population-based, observational cohort study initiated in 1948 to prospectively investigate the determinants of cardiovascular disease to guide public health prevention.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: The FHS began by recruiting an Original Cohort of 5,209 men and women between the ages of 30 and 62 from the town of Framingham, Massachusetts, who had not yet developed overt symptoms of cardiovascular disease or suffered a heart attack or stroke.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: The Original cohort Exam 1 took place between 1948 and 1953.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: Since that time the cohort has had a total of 32 biennial exams (ending in 2014) and event follow-up through 2022.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: In 1971, the FHS added the Offspring cohort, comprising 5124 children whose parents were enrolled in the Original cohort and the spouses of the children.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: This cohort on average has been examined every three to four years.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: However, there was an eight year gap between Exam 1 and Exam 2 and a seven year gap between Exam 7 and Exam 8.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: The latest exam (10) was completed in 2022.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: In 2002, the transgenerational FHS design was facilitated with the recruitment of 4095 children of the Offspring cohort (Third Generation), and 103 spouses of the Offspring who were not previously enrolled in the study (New Offspring Spouses, NOS).
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: These cohorts have completed 3 exams through 2019.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: To reflect the changing demographic characteristics of the greater Framingham community, the FHS additionally recruited and enrolled 2 cohorts comprising racial and ethnic minority groups, termed Omni-1 and Omni-2, (n = 506 and 410, respectively) in 1995 and 2002, respectively.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: These cohorts included individuals of African American, Hispanic, Asian, Indian, Native American, and Pacific Islander descent.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: The OMNI-1 cohort have completed 5 exams through 2022.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: The OMNI-2 cohort have completed 3 exams through 2019.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: Data available for request include Echocardiogram images, available from the following exams in each cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - Imaging

properties.page_content: Original Cohort: exams 18-32; Offspring cohort: exams 3-10; Third Generation, NOS and OMNI-2 cohorts: exams 1-3; OMNI-1 cohort: exams 1-5.CT image data at one or two timepoints were added for 4427 participants in the offspring, third generation, and OMNI1 and OMNI2 cohorts.Summary level phenotypes for the Framingham Cohort study participants can be viewed at the top-level study page phs000007 Framingham Cohort.

properties.page_content: Objectives The objectives of the Framingham Study are to study the incidence and prevalence of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and its risk factors, trends in CVD incidence and its risk factors over time, and familial patterns of CVD and risk factors.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Other important objectives include the estimation of incidence rates of disease and description of the natural history of cardiovascular disease, including the sequence of clinical signs and systems that precede the clinically recognizable syndrome and the consequences and course of clinically manifest disease.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Background Original cohort: The original cohort of the Framingham Study began in 1948 under the U.S.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Public Health Service and was transferred under the direct operations of the new National Heart Institute, NIH, in 1949.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Participants were sampled from Framingham, Massachusetts, including both men and women.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: This was the first prospective study of cardiovascular disease and identified the concept of risk factors and their joint effects.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Offspring/Omni1 cohort: With the aging of the Framingham cohort and with interest in familiar aggregation and heritability, a new cohort consisting of the offspring of the original cohort was sampled.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Spouses of offspring were also included.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: This new sample, began enrollment in 1971 and constituted a second generation of participants, permitting new assessment of risk factors and outcomes, and provided a resource for the genetic analyses which were yet to come.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: The Offspring participants have had repeated examinations, though at typically longer intervals than the original cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Third Generation/Omni2/New Offspring Cohort: Thirty-one years after enrollment began for the second generation of the Framingham Heart Study (Framingham Offspring Study), Framingham investigators began enrolling adults with at least one parent enrolled in the Offspring study into the Framingham Generation 3 cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: The addition of the third generation was expected to facilitate investigation of secular trends in risk factors and indicators of health and disease within families, to enhance statistical power to detect genetic and environmental determinants of complex diseases, and to clarify how subclinical cardiovascular disease predicts occurrence of overt clinical events.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Participants Original cohort: At entry to the study in 1948-1952, the study recruited 5,209 men and women, ages 28-62 years, living in Framingham, MA.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Offspring/Omni1 cohort: 5,124 men and women, ages 5-70 years at entry consisting of offspring of the original Framingham cohort (and spouses of the offspring).
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: In 1994, the Omni Cohort 1 enrolled 507 men and women of African-American, Hispanic, Asian, Indian, Pacific Islander and Native American origins, who at the time of enrollment were residents of Framingham and the surrounding towns.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Third Generation/Omni2/New Offspring Cohort: 4095 men and women, almost all who self reported their ethnicity as white, ages 19+ years at entry, with at least one parent in the Framingham Offspring study, participated in the Gen III cohort.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: The New Offspring Cohort enrolled spouses of Offspring participants that were not otherwise enrolled and had at least two biological children participating in Gen III.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: 103 New Offspring Spouses (47 men and 56 women) participated.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: The OMNI 2 cohort enrolled additional ethnically diverse participants, including many individuals related to the participants of Omni Cohort 1 and also individuals unrelated to Omni Cohort 1 members for a total of 410 new participants.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Design The cardiovascular disease conditions under investigation include coronary heart disease (angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, coronary insufficiency and sudden and non-sudden death), stroke, hypertension, peripheral arterial disease and congestive heart failure.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Original cohort: The Framingham Study is a longitudinal investigation of constitutional and environmental factors influencing the development of CVD in men and women.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Examination of participants has taken place every two years and the cohort has been followed for morbidity and mortality over that time period.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Offspring/Omni1 cohort: By 1975, a sample of 5,124 men and women, consisting of offspring of the original Framingham cohort (and spouses of the offspring) had participated in the study.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Additional studies of these subjects have continued under research contracts.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: Third Generation/Omni2/New Offspring Cohort: The children of Offspring Cohort participants were initially identified who would be 20 years of age or older by the end of the enrollment period.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC

properties.page_content: A higher priority for recruitment was assigned to individuals who belonged to large extended families, in order to complement phenotypic and genotypic information already obtained from prior generations.
properties.title: Framingham Heart Study-Cohort (FHS-Cohort) - BioLINCC
