properties.page_content: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC).
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Objectives We are sharing a database of dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) scans of normal children, which can serve as a reference standard to quantify regional respiratory abnormalities in young patients with various respiratory conditions and facilitate treatment planning and response assessment.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The database can also be useful to advance future AI-based research on image-based object segmentation and analysis.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Background In pediatric patients with respiratory abnormalities, it is important to understand the alterations in regional dynamics of the lungs and other thoracoabdominal components, which in turn requires a quantitative understanding of what is considered as normal in healthy children.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Currently, such a normative database of regional respiratory structure and function in healthy children does not exist.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Participants 200 normal children (ages 6-18 years) participated in our research study related to this dataset.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: DesignThe shared open-source normative database is from our ongoing virtual growing child (VGC) project, which includes 4D dMRI images representing one breathing cycle for each normal child and also segmentations of 10 objects at end expiration (EE) and end inspiration (EI) phases of the respiratory cycle in the 4D image.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The lung volumes at EE and EI as well as the excursion volumes of chest wall and diaphragm from EE to EI, left and right sides separately, are also reported.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The database has thus 4,000 3D segmentations from 200 normal children in total.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The database is unique and provides dMRI images, object segmentations, and quantitative regional respiratory measurement parameters of volumes for normal children.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: All dMRI scans are acquired from normal children during free-breathing.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The dMRI acquisition protocol was as follows: 3T MRI scanner (Verio, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany), true-FISP bright-blood sequence, TR=3.82 ms, TE=1.91 ms, voxel size ~1×1×6 mm3, 320×320 matrix, bandwidth 258 Hz, and flip angle 76o.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: With recent advances, for each sagittal location across the thorax and abdomen, we acquired 40 2D slices over several tidal breathing cycles at ~480 ms/slice.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: On average, 35 sagittal locations are imaged, yielding a total of ~1400 2D MRI slices, with a resulting total scan time of 11-13 minutes for any particular study participant.The collected dMRI scan data then went through the procedure of 4D image construction, image processing, object segmentation, and volumetric measurements from segmentations.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: 4D image construction: For the acquired dMRI scans, we utilized an automated 4D image construction approach to form one 4D image over one breathing cycle (consisting of typically 5-8 respiratory phases) from each acquired dMRI scan to represent the whole dynamic thoraco-abdominal body region.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The algorithm selects 175-280 slices (35 sagittal locations × 5-8 respiratory phases) from the 1400 acquired slices in an optimal manner using an optical flux method.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Image processing: Intensity standardization is performed on every time point/3D volume of the 4D image so that image values have the same tissue-specific meaning across all subjects.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Object segmentation: For each subject, there are 10 objects segmented at both EE and EI time points in this database.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: They include the thoracoabdominal skin outer boundary, left and right lungs, liver, spleen, left and right kidneys, diaphragm, and left and right hemi-diaphragms.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: All dMRI scans utilize large field of view images, which include the full thorax and abdomen to the inferior aspect of the kidneys in the sagittal plane.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: We used a pretrained U-Net based deep learning network to first segment all objects, and then all auto-segmentation results were visually checked and manually refined as needed, under the supervision of a radiologist with over 25 years of expertise in MRI and thoracoabdominal radiology.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Manual segmentations have been performed for all objects in all datasets.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: Volumetric measurements based on object segmentations for lung volumes (left and right separately) at EE and EI, as well as for chest wall and diaphragm excursion volumes (left and right separately) are reported.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: ConclusionsThe provided database is unique and provides dMRI images, object segmentations, and quantitative regional respiratory measurement parameters of volumes for normal children.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The database has 4,000 3D segmentations from 200 normal children, which to our knowledge is the largest and only such dMRI dataset to date.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: All images and object segmentations are saved in DICOM.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: All DICOM files (176,574 in total) have been anonymized, and PHI has been removed.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The database can be used as a reference standard to quantify regional respiratory abnormalities in young patients with various respiratory conditions and facilitate treatment planning and response assessment.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.page_content: The large amount of object segmentations can potentially benefit AI-based research on image-based object segmentation and analysis.
properties.title: Virtual Growing Child 5-Dimensional Functional Models for Treating Respiratory Anomalies (dMRI-VGC)

properties.title: INfluenza Vaccine to Effectively Stop Cardio Thoracic Events and Decompensated Heart Failure (INVESTED)

properties.page_content: INVESTED was planned as a large, adequately powered, multicenter trial to assess the cardiopulmonary benefit of high- compared with standard-dose influenza vaccine in a high-risk cardiovascular population.
properties.title: INfluenza Vaccine to Effectively Stop Cardio Thoracic Events and Decompensated Heart Failure (INVESTED)

properties.page_content: In contrast to more complex interventions in patients with cardiac disease, the major potential benefits of this intervention are a) the ease of administration, b) low cost, c) 100% vaccination adherence and d) well established and extremely low risk.
properties.title: INfluenza Vaccine to Effectively Stop Cardio Thoracic Events and Decompensated Heart Failure (INVESTED)

properties.page_content: This trial, if positive, has the potential to substantially impact a major population attributable CV risk, change practice, and inform health policy by boosting utilization of influenza vaccination.
properties.title: INfluenza Vaccine to Effectively Stop Cardio Thoracic Events and Decompensated Heart Failure (INVESTED)

properties.page_content: Stressors and Health Study. ObjectivesThe objectives of the Stressors and Health Study were to: (1) examine the prevalence of stressors and health outcomes and (2) assess differences in the associations between multi-level stressors and health outcomes, and (3) explore the protective and adaptive factors in the associations between multi-level stressors and health outcomes.
properties.title: Stressors and Health Study

properties.page_content: Background Stressors have been posited to explain disparities in health.
properties.title: Stressors and Health Study

properties.page_content: However, no surveys to our knowledge have simultaneously collected multiple stressors at various levels and the coping strategies used to deal with these stressors.
properties.title: Stressors and Health Study

properties.page_content: Measuring these factors can provide a better understanding of the stressors experienced by specific groups and the impact that these experiences have on their health and health practices.
properties.title: Stressors and Health Study

properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Objectives: The Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) was performed to identify suitable predictors of respiratory outcomes that may serve as surrogate endpoints in future trials of prevention and therapy of respiratory diseases in preterm infants.Background: Acute and chronic respiratory morbidities are common in premature births, and can pose significant risk to the infant's health, particularly during the first two years of life.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: One such condition is bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) where infants require oxygen therapy due to abnormal repair and impaired lung development after acute lung injury.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: BPD poses a high mortality risk, even in infants that survive the initial hospitalization.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Regardless of BPD diagnosis, preterm infants frequently return for medical care due to symptoms of post-prematurity respiratory disease (PRD), which includes intermittent or chronic wheezing, cough without cold, poor growth, apnea and cyanosis, and lower respiratory tract infections.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Impaired lung function can persist into adulthood, contributing to chronic respiratory diseases including asthma and emphysema.However, at the time of the PROP study, there were no objective measures to predict which preterm infants would have persistent respiratory problems after discharge from the hospital.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Furthermore, improved survival rates of premature infants and the high prevalence of lasting respiratory morbidities highlight the need for more comprehensive strategies to address both short-term and long-term respiratory complications.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Thus, the Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) was formed to investigate multiple research hypotheses on the molecular mechanisms that contribute to respiratory disease risk of premature neonates over the first year of life.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Specifically, PROP investigators hypothesized that in survivors of extreme prematurity to 36 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA), specific biologic, physiologic and clinical data obtained during the initial hospitalization will predict respiratory morbidity between discharge and 1 year corrected age.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants: A total of 835 infants were enrolled.Design: PROP was a collaboratively developed multicenter prospective cohort study of very preterm infants from birth through the time of discharge from the NICU and up to one year corrected age.Clinical data included maternal and infant demographics, co-morbidities, and daily infant respiratory, nutritional, and medication data until discharge.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: These were prospectively collected from birth using medical record review and family interviews.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: After discharge, phone interviews were conducted with the infant's main caregiver at 3, 6, 9 and 12 months corrected age to assess domains of respiratory morbidity.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: At 6 and 12 months corrected age, a survey of environmental respiratory irritant exposures and an assessment for gastroesophageal reflux disease were also completed.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A standardized physical exam was performed at 36-40 weeks PMA and again at one year corrected age.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The exam focused on anthropometrics, vital signs, and respiratory system signs.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: At 34-41 weeks PMA and within one week of anticipated discharge based on physiologic stability, a set of non-invasive respiratory assessments were performed to assess physiologic biomarkers in infants that were not mechanically ventilated or receiving non-invasive positive pressure ventilation.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Respiratory inductance plethysmography (RIP) was performed before and after inhaled albuterol to assess potential airway reactivity.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: During the RIP study, continuous pulse oximetry was performed during quiet sleep in order to analyze oxygen desaturations and apneas.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Standardized oxygen requirement challenge tests were performed at about 36 weeks PMA, and at about 40 weeks PMA if the infant was still hospitalized and was not eligible for, or failed, the previous challenge.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Failure was defined as SpO2 < 90% for 5 continuous minutes, SpO2 < 80% for 15 seconds, or apnea for >20 seconds at any point in the testing.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Infants breathing ambient air or that passed the 36 week challenge test underwent a hypoxia challenge consisting of a 15-minute trial of FiO2 of 0.15.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Failure was defined as SpO2 < 85% for 60 consecutive seconds, SpO2 < 80% for 15 seconds, bradycardia, or persistent apnea.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Infant pulmonary function testing (iPFT) was also performed on a subset of infants at one year corrected age to evaluate lung growth and respiratory dysfunction.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The primary outcome was respiratory morbidity, as measured by the presence or absence of substantial post-prematurity respiratory disease (PRD) up to one year corrected age.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: PRD was classified as a positive response in at least one of four morbidity domains during at least two separate parental interviews.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The domains were respiratory medications, hospitalizations for cardiopulmonary cause, respiratory symptoms, and home technology dependence (oxygen, ventilator, or CPAP/BiPAP).
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Mortality from a respiratory cause was also incorporated.
properties.title: Prematurity and Respiratory Outcomes Program (PROP) Core Database Protocol (PROP-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Data Access NOTE: Please refer to the "Authorized Access" section below for information about how access to the data from this accession differs from many other dbGaP accessions.Objectives: To compare treatment with sacubitril/valsartan versus valsartan alone in patients with advanced heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction and recent New York Heart Association class IV symptoms.Background: Treatment with evidence-based medical therapies improves survival, reduces heart failure hospitalizations, and improves quality of life in patients with chronic heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)
keyphrases: New York Heart Association class IV

properties.page_content: However, evidence supporting the use of medical therapies among patients with advanced heart failure is limited.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV heart failure are not often enrolled in clinical trials.A previous trial reported that, compared with the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor enalapril, sacubitril/valsartan, an angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, reduced the relative risk of cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalizations by 20% in ambulatory patients with heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)
keyphrases: New York Heart Association (NYHA) class IV heart failure

properties.page_content: Although patients with NYHA class IV heart failure were eligible to enroll, this population was underrepresented.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The HFN-LIFE trial was initiated to provide additional information about the tolerability, safety, and potential efficacy of sacubitril/valsartan in patients with advanced heart failure.Participants: Of the eligible patients that enrolled, a total of 335 patients tolerated the run-in phase and were randomized to a treatment group.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: 167 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacubitril/valsartan and 168 patients were randomly assigned to receive valsartan alone.Design: The HFN-LIFE trial was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind phase 4 clinical trial.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Trial enrollment was suspended early, due to the high risk for adverse outcomes associated with COVID-19 infection.Eligible patients were enrolled and began an unblinded run-in period of 3 to 7 days with sacubitril/valsartan, 24/26 mg (50-mg fixed dose), administered orally twice daily.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants tolerating the run-in phase were randomized in a 1:1 fashion to receive sacubitril/valsartan (target dose, 200 mg twice daily) or valsartan (target dose, 160 mg twice daily).
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The initial doses were selected based on guidelines with dose adjustments being made every 2 weeks.The primary efficacy outcome was the area under the curve of NT-proBNP levels at 2, 4, 8, 12, and 24 weeks compared with the level of NT-proBNP at randomization.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The secondary efficacy end point was the number of days the patient was alive, out of the hospital, and free from any of the following outcomes: listing for cardiac transplant, cardiac transplant, implantation of a left ventricular assist device, receipt of continuous inotropic therapy for 7 or more days, or hospitalization for heart failure on 2 or more occasions other than the index admission.Conclusions: In patients with chronic advanced heart failure with a reduced ejection fraction, there was no statistically significant difference between sacubitril/valsartan and valsartan alone with respect to reducing NT-proBNP levels.
properties.title: Heart Failure Network: Entresto(TM) in Advanced Heart Failure (HFN-LIFE-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC). Objectives: To investigate the early natural history of cardiovascular disease in a cohort of children and young adults in a biracial, semirural community.Background: The Bogalusa Heart Study has been a long-term epidemiologic study.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The investigators have identified and followed black and white participants for nearly 40 years, and have described the incidence and prevalence of biologic and behavioral cardiovascular disease risk factors from childhood through adulthood.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Their participation has enabled the study to not only document differences between males and females, but also between blacks and whites.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The results from the Bogalusa Heart Study have clearly documented that the genesis of atherosclerosis has its basis in childhood, and that prevention can and must begin at the early ages.The Bogalusa Heart Study had been funded over the years by the Specialized Centers of Research (SCOR) Program.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The SCOR program was initiated by NHLBI in 1970 to expedite the development and application of new knowledge essential for improved diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of arteriosclerosis, hypertension, pulmonary disease, and thrombosis.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: In 1984 a Demonstration and Education Component was added to the parent SCOR of the Bogalusa Heart Study in order to translate the experience gained in epidemiological studies into an intervention study designed to retard the development of cardiovascular risk factors in children.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Beginning in 1997, the study was supported by the cooperative agreement mechanism.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Participants: The Bogalusa dataset includes 11,796 participants that attended at least one of seven cross-sectional pediatric exams and/or the 1995-96 adult examination.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Subjects ranged in age from 3 to 20 years at the pediatric exams and 20-37 at the time of the adult exam.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Approximately 6,000 have more than one examination constituting a dynamic cohort.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Design: The initial survey in 1973-1974 was restricted to children ages 2 1/2 to 14.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: A physical examination was conducted and information was collected on anthropometric data, hemoglobin, blood pressure, serum lipids, and health history.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Over 3,500 children participated. The second cross-sectional survey of 1976-1977 and subsequent surveys expanded the eligible population to include all children ages 5-17 years.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The second survey of over 4,000 children also included information on salt intake, smoking, health beliefs, and attitudes, and for girls ages 8-17, menstrual history and oral contraceptive use.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The third survey of over 3,500 participants in 1978-1979 also collected anthropometric measurements on skinfold thickness and two measurements of heart rate.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The fourth survey of over 3,300 participants in 1981-1982 added data on alcohol use, Type A behavior, peer networks and dieting habits.The Bogalusa Heart Study continued to use a cross-sectional and longitudinal design with the general cross-sectional survey of approximately 3,700 Bogalusa children ages five to seventeen in 1988-1989 in the sixth screen and additional longitudinal studies to recall children in defined subgroups for more intensive evaluation.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Half of the 12,000 participants screened since 1973 had been studied three or more times.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The Post High School Study examined young adults ages 21 through 30 who previously were examined as children ages five through fourteen in the first Bogalusa Heart Study screening in 1973-1974.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The population included approximately 4,603 young adults originally screened and any other children or adolescents examined for the first time in any subsequent surveys.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: The cardiovascular phenotypes include obesity, blood pressure, lipids, lipoproteins, apoproteins, homocysteine, glucose-insulin, fibrinogen, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and von Willebrand Factor.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Environmental risk factors consist of sociodemographic characteristics, tobacco and alcohol use, oral contraception, physical activity, cognitive and physical function, and quality of sleep and diet.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)

properties.page_content: Subclinical morbidity includes echo-Doppler measurements of cardiac-carotid structure and function.
properties.title: Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS-BioLINCC)
